## 1013. test_conditions_on_observations

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/inference/test_map_runner.py:129](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/inference/test_map_runner.py:129)

```python
def test_conditions_on_observations(beta_binomial_graph: BayesGraph) -> None:
    """The estimate responds to evidence: it lands at the analytic posterior.

    We don't fit the prior-only model here -- with no evidence the Binomial
    node is an *unobserved discrete latent*, which SVI would try to enumerate
    (a funsor path we don't depend on). The prior mode is known analytically
    (Beta(2,2) -> 0.5), so we condition and check the estimate moved onto the
    posterior mode (Beta(16,8) -> 15/22 ~ 0.682), clear of the prior.
    """
    model = compile_model(beta_binomial_graph)
    conditioned = run_map(
        model,
        beta_binomial_graph,
        Observations(by_site={"k": OBSERVED_K}),
        steps=1500,
    )
    theta_obs = conditioned.posterior["theta"].values.item()
    posterior_mode = (PRIOR_ALPHA + OBSERVED_K - 1) / (
        PRIOR_ALPHA + PRIOR_BETA + N_TRIALS - 2
    )  # 15 / 22 ~ 0.682
    assert abs(theta_obs - posterior_mode) < 0.03
    assert theta_obs > 0.5 + 0.1  # clearly shifted up from the prior mode
```

```python
def test_serializes_to_netcdf(axed_graph: BayesGraph, tmp_path) -> None:

    np.testing.assert_array_equal(
        reloaded["posterior"].to_dataset()["segment_shares"].values,
        result.posterior["segment_shares"].values,
    )
```

```python
def _register_root() -> None:
    """Parentless deterministic root; indicator code unlike its node id.

    The constructor never mentions ``node_id`` -- that it comes out attributed
    anyway is exactly what is under test.
    """

    def root(
        resolved_bindings: Mapping[str, tuple[StructuredArray, ...]],
        *,
        sample_fn: SampleFn,
        deterministic_fn: DeterministicFn,
        hyperparameters: Mapping[str, Any],
        name: str,
    ) -> StructuredArray:
        del resolved_bindings, sample_fn, hyperparameters
        value = deterministic_fn(name, jnp.array([1.0, 2.0]))
        return StructuredArray(
            array=value,
            axes=(GENDER,),
            indicator=IndicatorMeta(indicator="income", family="rate", unit="rate"),
            population=None,
        )

    register_cpd(
        "testutil",
        "root",
        root,
        kind="deterministic",
        parameter_schema={},
        hyperparameter_schema={},
        resolve_bindings=lambda *, child, parents, hyperparameters: {},
    )
```

## 1038. _register_recorder

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/inference/test_node_id_attribution.py:91](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/inference/test_node_id_attribution.py:91)

```python
def _register_recorder() -> None:
    """Deterministic child that records what its single parent arrived as."""

    def recorder(
        resolved_bindings: Mapping[str, tuple[StructuredArray, ...]],
        *,
        sample_fn: SampleFn,
        deterministic_fn: DeterministicFn,
        hyperparameters: Mapping[str, Any],
        name: str,
    ) -> StructuredArray:
        del sample_fn, hyperparameters
        parent = resolved_bindings["param"][0]
        SEEN[name] = (parent.node_id, parent.indicator.indicator)
        return StructuredArray(
            array=deterministic_fn(name, parent.array),
            axes=parent.axes,
            indicator=IndicatorMeta(indicator="downstream", family="rate", unit="rate"),
            population=None,
        )

    register_cpd(
        "testutil",
        "recorder",
        recorder,
        kind="deterministic",
        parameter_schema={
            "param": ParamDecl(description="Single parent.", min_count=1, max_count=1),
        },
        hyperparameter_schema={},
        resolve_bindings=lambda *, child, parents, hyperparameters: {
            "param": tuple(p.node_id for p in parents)
        },
    )
```

```python
def _run() -> dict:
    g = BayesGraph()
    g.add_node(_node("income_z", "root"))
    g.add_node(_node("child", "recorder", param=("income_z",)))
    g.add_edge("income_z", "child")
    model = compile_model(g)
    with numpyro.handlers.seed(rng_seed=0):
        return model()
```

```python
def test_the_two_keys_travel_separately() -> None:
    """Node id and indicator code are independent -- the whole point of the split.

    ``income_z`` advertises the indicator code ``income`` (a standardizer reports
    the sheet its parent was read from) while being the node ``income_z``. Under
    the old single-key regime the matching sites read a node id out of the
    indicator slot, which worked only while the two happened to agree.
```

## 1054. _sampled

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/inference/test_output.py:32](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/inference/test_output.py:32)

```python
def _sampled(posterior, dims, coords, families=None):
    """A node->StructuredArray map from arrays given with their dims and coords.

    The arrays arrive with the ``(chain, draw)`` prefix a container carries; a
    ``StructuredArray`` has one dim per declared axis and no sample dims, so the
    prefix is reshaped away here.
    """
    families = families or {}
    out = {}
    for node_id, array in posterior.items():
        names = dims.get(node_id, [])
        family, unit = families.get(node_id, ("rate", "1"))
        out[node_id] = StructuredArray(
            array=np.asarray(array).reshape([len(coords[name]) for name in names]),
            axes=tuple(
                AxisMeta(name=name, levels=tuple(coords[name]), kind="categorical")
                for name in names
            ),
            indicator=IndicatorMeta(indicator=node_id, family=family, unit=unit),
            population=None,
        )
    return out
```

## 1055. _make_result

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/inference/test_output.py:70](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/inference/test_output.py:70)

```python
def _make_result(
    *,
    with_population: bool = True,
    losses=None,
    shares_name: str = "segment_shares",
    pop_name: str = "population",
) -> InferenceResult:
    """A single-draw ``InferenceResult`` over the synthetic cross-section."""
    shares = np.array([_SHARES[c] for c in _COUNTRIES])  # (country, segment)
    shares = shares[:, np.newaxis, :]  # (country, year, segment)
    posterior = {shares_name: shares[np.newaxis, np.newaxis, ...]}
    dims = {shares_name: ["country", "year", "segment"]}
    if with_population:
        pop = np.array([_POPULATION[c] for c in _COUNTRIES])[:, np.newaxis]
        posterior[pop_name] = pop[np.newaxis, np.newaxis, ...]
        dims[pop_name] = ["country", "year"]
    coords = {
        "country": list(_COUNTRIES),
        "year": [_YEAR],
        "segment": list(_SEGMENTS),
    }
    families = {pop_name: ("count", "people")}
    return InferenceResult(
        _sampled(posterior, dims, coords, families), losses=losses
    )
```

## 1068. _make_param_result

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/inference/test_output.py:263](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/inference/test_output.py:263)

```python
def _make_param_result() -> InferenceResult:
    posterior = {
        "kappa": np.array(40.0).reshape(1, 1),  # scalar node (chain, draw)
        "bias": np.array([0.1, 0.2, 0.3])[np.newaxis, np.newaxis, :],  # 1-D
        "weight": _WEIGHT[np.newaxis, np.newaxis, ...],  # 2-D
        "shares": np.array(  # 3-D (country, year, segment)
            [_SHARES[c] for c in ("CCC", "AAA")]
        )[:, np.newaxis, :][np.newaxis, np.newaxis, ...],
    }
    dims = {
        "bias": ["transition"],
        "weight": ["transition", "driver"],
        "shares": ["country", "year", "segment"],
    }
    coords = {
        "transition": list(_TRANSITIONS),
        "driver": list(_DRIVERS),
        "country": ["CCC", "AAA"],
        "year": [_YEAR],
        "segment": list(_SEGMENTS),
    }
    return InferenceResult(_sampled(posterior, dims, coords))
```

```python
def test_sheet_names_are_excel_safe_and_unique(tmp_path) -> None:
    """19. Forbidden chars stripped, length capped, truncation collisions broken."""
    clash_a = "a" * 40 + "/one"  # truncates to 31 'a's ...
    clash_b = "a" * 40 + "/two"  # ... same prefix -> must be de-duplicated
    tables = {
        "bad:name*here": pd.DataFrame({"value": [1]}),
        clash_a: pd.DataFrame({"value": [2]}),
        clash_b: pd.DataFrame({"value": [3]}),
        output.SHEET_RUN_INFO: pd.DataFrame({"key": ["k"], "value": [1]}),
    }
    path = output.write_workbook(tables, tmp_path, now=datetime(2026, 6, 9, 1, 2, 3))
    names = pd.ExcelFile(path).sheet_names
    assert len(set(names)) == len(names)  # unique
    for name in names:
        assert len(name) <= 31
        assert not (set(name) & set('[]:*?/\\'))
    assert output.SHEET_RUN_INFO in names  # short, legal names pass through
```

```python
def test_indicator_and_axis_role_survive_the_round_trip(tmp_path) -> None:
    """What schema 1 could not promise back.

    A result that reloaded with the right numbers under the wrong ``family``
    would aggregate wrongly and still compare equal, which is why ``__eq__``
    now looks at the metadata and why this test is a round trip rather than a
    manifest inspection. The two nodes differ in both fields so a writer that
    stamped one node's metadata onto every node would fail here.
    """
    result = _result(
        {
            "shares": _roled([0.4, 0.6], "segment", ("low", "high"), "segmentation"),
            "people": _roled(
                [10.0, 20.0], "year", (2019, 2020), "time",
                family="count", unit="people",
            ),
        }
    )
    loaded = load_result(save_result(result, tmp_path))
    assert loaded == result
    shares = loaded.structured("shares")
    assert shares.axes[0].axis_role == "segmentation"
    assert shares.axes[0].kind == "ordinal"
    assert loaded.structured("people").indicator.family == "count"
```

```python
def test_a_population_pointer_is_refused_rather_than_dropped(tmp_path) -> None:
    """The ≤v3 demo sets one (``demo_v0.yaml``'s ``from_data`` weights, on
    ``income`` alone), and the writer has no form for it: the array is loaded
    data, not a node, so there is nothing to reference. Refusing keeps the
    bijection true; writing a file that reads back without the pointer would
    not."""
    people = _sa(np.array([10.0], dtype=np.float32), [("year", (2019,))], family="count")
    weighted = StructuredArray(
```

```python
    assert loaded.node_for_special("population") == "people"

    assert loaded.node_for_special("nothing_marks_this") is None
```

```python
def test_structured_attaches_the_population_from_the_special() -> None:
    """Where a finished result's population comes from.

    Not from a pointer baked in at build time: the v4 graph wires the population
    as a *parent* of each observation grid, for the grid to collapse an axis
    with, and the emitted array's pointer stays ``None``. The special is what
    lets a consumer holding only the result find the people.
    """
    result = InferenceResult(
        _two_node().sampled(), specials={"people": ("population",)}
    )
    rate = result.structured("rate")
    assert rate.population is not None
    assert rate.population.node_id == "people"
    assert rate.population.indicator.family == "count"
    # Verbatim, at the population's own axes -- projecting it onto this node's
    # is the reduction's business (see `core.structured_array`).
    assert rate.population.axis_names == ("country",)
```

```python
def _wrap_scalar(value: Any) -> StructuredArray:
    """Wrap a 0-d JAX array in a minimal StructuredArray scaffold.

    Axes are empty (ndim 0 matches len(axes) 0); indicator family is
    ``rate`` purely so it passes ``IndicatorMeta`` validation -- nothing
    in these tests calls a reduction that would actually consult the
    family or population pointer.

    The ``jnp.asarray`` cast is belt-and-suspenders: the production
    ``sample_fn`` / ``deterministic_fn`` wrappers in
    ``inference/compile.py`` already normalize their returns to JAX
    arrays, so a real CPD body wouldn't need this. Keeping it here
    means the scaffold stays robust if a future test plumbs a raw
    Python scalar through some other path.
    """
    return StructuredArray(
        array=jnp.asarray(value),
        axes=(),
        indicator=IndicatorMeta(indicator="test", family="rate", unit="unitless"),
        population=None,
    )
```

## 1118. _stochastic_cpd

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/inference/test_sample_wrapper.py:83](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/inference/test_sample_wrapper.py:83)

```python
def _stochastic_cpd(
    resolved_bindings: Mapping[str, tuple[StructuredArray, ...]],
    *,
    sample_fn: Any,
    deterministic_fn: Any,
    hyperparameters: Mapping[str, Any],
    name: str,
) -> StructuredArray:
    """A D21-compliant stochastic CPD: one ``sample_fn`` call, no parents.

    Samples from a Beta(2, 2) at the canonical site ``name``. The Beta
    choice is arbitrary -- bounded support on [0, 1] just makes
    intervene-value assertions easy to write (any number in [0, 1]
    is a plausible "real" sample, so the test's intervention value
    isn't obviously distinguishable by domain alone, only by trace
    metadata).
    """
    del resolved_bindings, deterministic_fn, hyperparameters
    value = sample_fn(name, dist.Beta(2.0, 2.0))
    return _wrap_scalar(value)
```

## 1119. _deterministic_cpd

[tests/inference/test_sample_wrapper.py:105](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/inference/test_sample_wrapper.py:105)

```python
def _deterministic_cpd(
    resolved_bindings: Mapping[str, tuple[StructuredArray, ...]],
    *,
    sample_fn: Any,
    deterministic_fn: Any,
    hyperparameters: Mapping[str, Any],
    name: str,
) -> StructuredArray:
    """A D21-compliant deterministic CPD: doubles its single parent.

    Reads role ``x`` (arity 1), multiplies the parent's array by 2,
    records the result via ``deterministic_fn``, and returns the wrapped
    value. Used to test the deterministic-fn intervene branch and the
    obs-on-deterministic rejection.
    """
    del sample_fn, hyperparameters
    parent = resolved_bindings["x"][0]
    value = parent.array * 2.0
    deterministic_fn(name, value)
    return _wrap_scalar(value)
```

## 1120. _shaped_cpd

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/inference/test_sample_wrapper.py:127](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/inference/test_sample_wrapper.py:127)

```python
def _shaped_cpd(
    resolved_bindings: Mapping[str, tuple[StructuredArray, ...]],
    *,
    sample_fn: Any,
    deterministic_fn: Any,
    hyperparameters: Mapping[str, Any],
    name: str,
) -> StructuredArray:
    """A stochastic CPD whose site has a non-trivial ``batch_shape`` of ``(3, 2)``.

    The scalar CPDs above cannot exercise A2's fill rules at all: a fill's whole
    claim is that it produces an array of *the site's* shape without having been
    told that shape, and every shape agrees with ``()``. Bernoulli is the family
    the real constraint sinks use, and ``obs=0`` on it is the same synthetic
    "no violation seen" evidence.
    """
    del resolved_bindings, deterministic_fn, hyperparameters
    value = sample_fn(name, dist.Bernoulli(probs=jnp.full((3, 2), 0.5)))
    return _wrap_shaped(value, (3, 2))
```

```python
def _event_dim_cpd(
    resolved_bindings: Mapping[str, tuple[StructuredArray, ...]],
    *,
    sample_fn: Any,
    deterministic_fn: Any,
    hyperparameters: Mapping[str, Any],
    name: str,
) -> StructuredArray:
    """A stochastic CPD with ``batch_shape == (3,)`` and ``event_shape == (4,)``.

    Dirichlet is the smallest family in the repo where the two differ, which is
    exactly the case that distinguishes filling to ``batch_shape`` from filling
    to the shape of one observation.
    """
    del resolved_bindings, deterministic_fn, hyperparameters
    value = sample_fn(name, dist.Dirichlet(jnp.full((3, 4), 1.0)))
    return _wrap_shaped(value, (3, 4))
```

## 1122. _wrap_shaped

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/inference/test_sample_wrapper.py:167](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/inference/test_sample_wrapper.py:167)

```python
def _wrap_shaped(value: Any, shape: tuple[int, ...]) -> StructuredArray:
    """``_wrap_scalar``'s shaped sibling: one categorical axis per dimension.

    The axis names and levels carry no meaning here -- ``StructuredArray``
    requires ``len(axes) == ndim``, and nothing in these tests reduces over
    them.
    """
    axes = tuple(
        AxisMeta(name=f"d{i}", levels=tuple(range(n)), kind="categorical")
        for i, n in enumerate(shape)
    )
    return StructuredArray(
        array=jnp.asarray(value, dtype=float).reshape(shape),
        axes=axes,
        indicator=IndicatorMeta(indicator="test", family="rate", unit="unitless"),
        population=None,
    )
```

## 1123. _resolve_x_parent

[tests/inference/test_sample_wrapper.py:186](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/inference/test_sample_wrapper.py:186)

```python
def _resolve_x_parent(
    *, child: NodeMeta, parents: tuple[NodeMeta, ...], hyperparameters: Mapping[str, Any]
) -> Mapping[str, tuple[str, ...]]:
    """Trivial role resolver: bind the single parent to role ``x``."""
    del child, hyperparameters
    if len(parents) != 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"_deterministic_cpd expects exactly one parent, got {len(parents)}"
        )
    return {"x": (parents[0].node_id,)}
```

```python
@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _setup_registry():
    """Register the in-test CPDs around each test, then clear.

    Mirrors the pattern in the end-to-end suites: ``test_cpd.py`` has an
    autouse teardown that clears the registry, so we set up explicitly
    here and leave the registry empty on exit.
    """
    _clear_registry()
    register_cpd(
        family="test_stochastic",
        constructor="prior",
        fn=_stochastic_cpd,
        kind="stochastic",
    )
    register_cpd(
        family="test_deterministic",
        constructor="latent",
        fn=_deterministic_cpd,
        kind="deterministic",
        parameter_schema={"x": ParamDecl(description="single parent")},
        resolve_bindings=_resolve_x_parent,
    )
    register_cpd(
        family="test_shaped",
        constructor="prior",
        fn=_shaped_cpd,
        kind="stochastic",
    )
    register_cpd(
        family="test_event_dims",
        constructor="prior",
        fn=_event_dim_cpd,
        kind="stochastic",
    )
    yield
    _clear_registry()
```

```python
def test_free_sample_routes_to_numpyro_sample(
    single_stochastic_graph: BayesGraph,
) -> None:
    """No observations, no interventions: site appears as a free sample.

    NumPyro's trace records each primitive call as a message; the
    ``type`` field is the dispatch tag (``"sample"`` for stochastic,
    ``"deterministic"`` for forced values). With nothing overriding,
    we expect a sample site that's not observed.
    """
    model = compile_model(single_stochastic_graph)
    with numpyro.handlers.seed(rng_seed=0):
        with numpyro.handlers.trace() as tr:
            model()
    assert tr["x"]["type"] == "sample"
    assert tr["x"]["is_observed"] is False
```

```python
def test_intervene_on_stochastic_routes_to_deterministic(
    single_stochastic_graph: BayesGraph,
) -> None:
    """``Interventions(by_site={"x": v})`` should rewrite x's site to deterministic.

    The do-operator semantics: the value is forced, the distribution
    is bypassed entirely (no log-prob factor enters the model). In the
    trace this surfaces as a site of ``type == "deterministic"`` --
    NumPyro's deterministic primitive doesn't accept an ``obs=`` kwarg
    and doesn't contribute to the log density.
    """
    model = compile_model(single_stochastic_graph)
    with numpyro.handlers.seed(rng_seed=0):
        with numpyro.handlers.trace() as tr:
            model(interventions=Interventions(by_site={"x": 0.7}))
    assert tr["x"]["type"] == "deterministic"
    assert float(tr["x"]["value"]) == pytest.approx(0.7)
```

```python
def test_intervene_on_deterministic_overrides_value(
    stochastic_then_deterministic_graph: BayesGraph,
) -> None:
    """Interventions are valid on deterministic CPDs too.

    Without the intervention, ``y == 2 * x`` (the in-test deterministic
    CPD doubles its parent). With ``Interventions(by_site={"y": v})``,
    the deterministic_fn's intervene branch substitutes ``v`` -- the
    parent-derived value is discarded. This is a real do-operation:
    consumers of y downstream would see v rather than 2*x.
    """
    model = compile_model(stochastic_then_deterministic_graph)
    with numpyro.handlers.seed(rng_seed=0):
        with numpyro.handlers.trace() as tr:
            model(interventions=Interventions(by_site={"y": 0.5}))
    assert tr["y"]["type"] == "deterministic"
    assert float(tr["y"]["value"]) == pytest.approx(0.5)
    # And x is untouched -- the intervention on y doesn't ripple upward.
    assert tr["x"]["type"] == "sample"
    assert tr["x"]["is_observed"] is False
```

```python
    but downstream CPDs still consume the (now forced) parent value.
```

```python
def test_obs_on_deterministic_raises(
    stochastic_then_deterministic_graph: BayesGraph,
) -> None:
    """Observations on deterministic sites have no NumPyro primitive.

    ``numpyro.deterministic`` doesn't accept ``obs=``, and the semantics
    would be ambiguous anyway (a deterministic value is fixed by its
    parents -- "observing" it either agrees with the parent-derived
    value or contradicts it, neither of which is useful). The wrapper
    rejects this up front rather than letting NumPyro raise a more
    confusing error deeper in.
    """
    model = compile_model(stochastic_then_deterministic_graph)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="deterministic"):
        model(observations=Observations(by_site={"y": 0.5}))
```

```python
def test_observe_and_intervene_collision_raises(
    single_stochastic_graph: BayesGraph,
) -> None:
    """A site can be observed XOR intervened upon, never both at once.

    The two are semantically distinct: an observation contributes
    ``log p(value | parents)`` to the posterior (evidence about a
    stochastic quantity), while an intervention severs the parent
    linkage and contributes nothing. Allowing both on the same site
    at the same step would be ambiguous, so the wrapper rejects the
    combination.
    """
    model = compile_model(single_stochastic_graph)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="both observed and intervened"):
        model(
            observations=Observations(by_site={"x": 0.3}),
            interventions=Interventions(by_site={"x": 0.7}),
        )
```

```python
def test_unknown_obs_site_is_silently_ignored(
    single_stochastic_graph: BayesGraph,
) -> None:
    """Obs ids that don't match any node in the model should not error.

    Rationale (see ``_build_sample_fn`` docstring): callers like the
    data ingester may legitimately produce ``Observations`` that
    out-scope the current compiled subgraph -- e.g. a master indicator
    table that includes ids for nodes not present in this particular
    model build. Rejecting would force every caller to pre-filter; the
    wrapper just drops unknowns instead.
    """
    model = compile_model(single_stochastic_graph)
    with numpyro.handlers.seed(rng_seed=0):
        with numpyro.handlers.trace() as tr:
            # "x" is real; "ghost" is not. Should not error.
            model(observations=Observations(by_site={"ghost": 0.42}))
    # x still samples freely -- the unknown obs key had no effect.
    assert tr["x"]["type"] == "sample"
    assert tr["x"]["is_observed"] is False
```

## 1141. test_fill_rule_conditions_at_the_sites_own_shape

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/inference/test_sample_wrapper.py:541](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/inference/test_sample_wrapper.py:541)

```python
def test_fill_rule_conditions_at_the_sites_own_shape(shaped_graph: BayesGraph) -> None:
    """The property A2 exists to establish, driven end to end through the wrapper.

    The rule is built from a site name and a constant. It is never told ``(3, 2)``
    -- the wrapper reads that off the distribution at the conditioning point. The
    array is therefore *built* to the right shape rather than checked against it,
    which is why the silent-broadcast hazard disappears on this path instead of
    being guarded (a scalar ``0.0`` passed as ``obs`` today broadcasts happily and
    NumPyro says nothing).
    """
    model = compile_model(shaped_graph)
    with numpyro.handlers.seed(rng_seed=0):
        with numpyro.handlers.trace() as tr:
            model(observations=Observations(rules=(obs_rules.fill({"s"}, 0.0),)))
    assert tr["s"]["is_observed"] is True
    assert tr["s"]["value"].shape == (3, 2)
    assert float(jnp.sum(tr["s"]["value"])) == 0.0
```

## 1142. test_fill_rule_covers_event_dims_too

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/inference/test_sample_wrapper.py:560](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/inference/test_sample_wrapper.py:560)

```python
def test_fill_rule_covers_event_dims_too(event_dim_graph: BayesGraph) -> None:
    """A fill spans ``batch_shape + event_shape``, not ``batch_shape`` alone.

    The spec wrote ``dist.batch_shape``, which is right for every constraint sink
    we have (Bernoulli, so ``event_shape == ()``) but not in general: one
    observation of a Dirichlet site is a ``(4,)`` simplex vector, so the array
    NumPyro wants is ``(3, 4)``. Filling only the batch dims would hand it a
    ``(3,)`` array, which is exactly the broadcast-shaped wrongness A3 goes on to
    reject on the literal path.
    """
    model = compile_model(event_dim_graph)
    with numpyro.handlers.seed(rng_seed=0):
        with numpyro.handlers.trace() as tr:
            model(observations=Observations(rules=(obs_rules.fill({"s"}, 0.25),)))
    assert tr["s"]["value"].shape == (3, 4)
```

## 1143. test_scalar_literal_is_rejected_at_the_conditioning_point

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/inference/test_sample_wrapper.py:577](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/inference/test_sample_wrapper.py:577)

```python
def test_scalar_literal_is_rejected_at_the_conditioning_point(
    shaped_graph: BayesGraph,
) -> None:
    """A3 end to end, on the path A2 could not make safe by construction.

    A fill given this same site builds a ``(3, 2)`` array and is right by
    construction. A literal holding ``0.0`` instead reaches all six cells by
    replication, NumPyro accepts it silently, and the trace then reports six
    observations where there was one number. The rejection has to happen where
    the shape is known, which is here.

    Worth recording what today actually does on *this* graph, since it is not
    quite the silent pass the hazard is usually described as: the scalar is
    accepted at the site and then blows up further downstream as a JAX reshape
    ``TypeError`` (``shape () (size 1) into shape (3, 2)``) inside a consuming
    CPD. So the failure exists but is remote from its cause, and names neither
    the site nor the evidence. Being told at the point of conditioning that a
    scalar cannot be evidence about six cells is the difference A3 makes.
    """
    model = compile_model(shaped_graph)
    with numpyro.handlers.seed(rng_seed=0):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="s"):
            model(observations=Observations(rules=(obs_rules.literal("s", 0.0),)))
```

```python
) -> None:
    """Enumerability is load-bearing, and this is the test that shows it.

    The pre-flight checks run *before* tracing, so they never see a shape and can
    never resolve a fill to a value -- they only need the set of claimed sites.
    That is the whole reason A2 uses a rule object rather than the closure form
    Max floated: a closure can only be interrogated by guessing names at it, so
    this error would silently stop being raised.

    model = compile_model(stochastic_then_deterministic_graph)
```

```python
def _node(node_id: str, role: str, *, shape: bool = True) -> dict[str, object]:
    """A minimal node carrying `role`.

    `shape=False` omits the `axes` hyperparameter, which matters for any pin
    asserted through desugar: a node that declares `axes` is the full-spec escape
    hatch (`desugar.py:2327`) and is left verbatim, so a shape pin written over
    the default `_node` would pass or fail for reasons having nothing to do with
    its role.
    """
    hyperparameters: dict[str, object] = {"alpha": 1.0, "beta": 1.0}
    if shape:
        hyperparameters["axes"] = ["country"]
    return {
        "id": node_id,
        "indicator": node_id,
        "role": role,
        "cpd": {
            "family": "beta",
            "constructor": "prior",
            "hyperparameters": hyperparameters,
        },
    }
```

```python
def _cfg(*nodes: dict[str, object], **extra: object) -> dict[str, object]:
    """A v4 config with one plain axis and one demographic one.

    `sex` is flagged `demographic_disagg` so that there is a complement for a
    `default_disagg` role to pull; without one, "inherits its parent's shaping"
    and "does nothing" are indistinguishable.
    """
    return {
        "version": 4,
        "axes": {
            "country": {"kind": "categorical", "levels": ["US", "GB"]},
            "sex": {
                "kind": "categorical",
                "levels": ["f", "m"],
                "demographic_disagg": True,
            },
        },
        "nodes": list(nodes),
        "edges": [],
        **extra,
    }
```

```python
def test_an_unrecognized_role_is_rejected() -> None:
    """A role in neither the defaults nor `node_roles:` is an error, not a shrug.

    Today `role` is a free string, so `resolve_role` returns
    ``"latnet_indicator"`` and every set membership test quietly answers False:
    the node gets no complement axes, no observations, and no diagnostic. A
    typo'd role is the cheapest possible mistake to make and currently the most
    expensive to notice, which is the whole argument for a validated universe.

    **Unmarked as of B2 step 2** (`node_roles:` on `GraphConfig`, with the
    unknown-role validator). Note what the validator checks: only the
    author-written `node.role`, not `resolve_role`'s output. A registry-derived
    role is knowledge `schema.py` cannot see -- the registry may not be
    populated -- and every such role is a built-in by construction, so a typo can
    only enter through the hand-written field.
    """
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        GraphConfig.model_validate(_cfg(_node("cov_3g", "latnet_indicator")))
```

## 1150. test_the_default_section_reproduces_the_current_frozensets

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_b2_node_roles.py:131](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_b2_node_roles.py:131)

```python
def test_the_default_section_reproduces_the_current_frozensets() -> None:
    """"Existing configs unchanged by construction" as a test, not a claim.

    B2 is a refactor wearing a feature's clothes: the section has to *say* what
    the code already does before anything is allowed to depend on it saying
    something else. Each frozenset is one question's current answer, so this
    checks all three of the questions that have an implementation today. The two
    that do not -- `unique` and `special` -- have nothing to compare against and
    are pinned by their own tests instead.

    Imported inside the body deliberately: at module scope the missing name would
    have been a collection error and would have taken the other three pins in this
    file down with it, reporting nothing about their subjects. Kept inside the body
    now that the names exist, so the reason stays legible.

    **Unmarked as of B2 step 1** (the spec and the derived frozensets), which is
    the whole of this pin's subject even though the config surface is still to
    come. Left `@needs("B2", ImportError)` it would be a strict XPASS.

    Note what this can and cannot prove. `COMPLEMENT_ROLES` contains `population`,
    which no constructor registers and no example config hand-writes, so a third
    of it has never been exercised. Reproducing it member-for-member is still the
    right refactor, but for that member the pin checks consistency with an
    intention rather than with observed behavior.
    """
    from digital_readiness.io.config.desugar import (  # noqa: PLC0415
        COMPLEMENT_ROLES,
        DEFAULT_NODE_ROLES,
        INHERIT_ROLES,
        _INDICATOR_INHERITING_ROLES,
    )

    axes = {r for r, spec in DEFAULT_NODE_ROLES.items() if spec.axes == "default_disagg"}
    assert axes == set(COMPLEMENT_ROLES)

    inherit = {r for r, spec in DEFAULT_NODE_ROLES.items() if spec.axes == "inherit"}
    assert inherit == set(INHERIT_ROLES)

    inheriting = {
        r for r, spec in DEFAULT_NODE_ROLES.items() if spec.indicator_inheritance
    }
    assert inheriting == set(_INDICATOR_INHERITING_ROLES)
```

```python
def test_a_declared_role_inherits_its_parents_answers_and_overrides_one() -> None:
    """`instance_of` composes, one level, with per-key override.

    The motivating case is the shipped pair: `population` *is* a latent
    indicator that additionally has a special property. Writing that as
    ``instance_of: indicator_latent`` plus the one differing key is the whole
    reason the section beats five parallel frozensets -- otherwise declaring a
    new role means remembering every set it belongs to.

    Asserted through desugar rather than against the section, because what an
    author cares about is that the *node* comes out shaped like its parent role.
    A derived role that validates but bakes no complement axes would pass a
    section-level check and still be broken.

    **Unmarked as of B2 step 3** (the readers ask `resolved_node_roles()`). Two
    things had to change for this, and it is worth keeping them apart: the
    schema half (`instance_of` resolution) landed at step 2 and this pin still
    failed, because `_bake_shape_axes` consulted the module-level
    `COMPLEMENT_ROLES` -- which by construction cannot contain a config-declared
    role. The frozenset being *derived* from the section was necessary and not
    sufficient; the reader had to be threaded to the config too.
    """
    cfg = GraphConfig.model_validate(
        _cfg(
            _node("cov_3g", "coverage_latent", shape=False),
            node_roles={
                "coverage_latent": {"instance_of": "indicator_latent", "unique": True}
            },
        )
    )
    (node,) = desugar(cfg).nodes

    # Inherited from `indicator_latent`: the demographic complement was baked.
    assert node.cpd is not None
    assert "sex" in tuple(node.cpd.hyperparameters["axes"])

    # And the overridden key took effect, so a second one would be refused.
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        GraphConfig.model_validate(
            _cfg(
                _node("cov_3g", "coverage_latent"),
                _node("cov_4g", "coverage_latent"),
                node_roles={
                    "coverage_latent": {
                        "instance_of": "indicator_latent",
                        "unique": True,
                    }
                },
            )
        )
```

## 1152. test_an_empty_special_unsets_the_shipped_one

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

```python
def test_an_empty_special_unsets_the_shipped_one() -> None:
    """``special: []`` is a stated empty, not an omission.

    Declaring a role *adds to* the registry, so a config naming its own
    population role would otherwise leave two roles carrying the special and let
    a consumer that looks it up find the wrong node. Writing the empty list on
    the built-in is how the special moves rather than duplicates -- the override
    filter keys on "not stated", and an empty list is stated.
    """
    from digital_readiness.core.graph import POPULATION_SPECIAL

    def carriers(cfg: GraphConfig) -> set[str]:
        return {
            name
            for name, spec in cfg.resolved_node_roles().items()
            if POPULATION_SPECIAL in spec.special
        }

    shipped = GraphConfig.model_validate(_cfg(_node("cov_3g", "indicator_latent")))
    assert carriers(shipped) == {"population"}

    moved = GraphConfig.model_validate(
        _cfg(
            _node("folks", "headcount"),
            node_roles={
                "headcount": {
                    "instance_of": "indicator_latent",
                    "special": ["population"],
                },
                "population": {"special": []},
            },
        )
    )
    assert carriers(moved) == {"headcount"}
```

## 1154. test_node_roles_is_refused_below_v4

```python
def test_node_roles_is_refused_below_v4() -> None:
    """The key is refused under `version: 3`, not ignored.

    The distinction is the whole point, and it is why this gate guards *meaning*
    rather than a no-op: `_bake_shape_axes` is deliberately not version-gated, so
    a `node_roles:` block in a v3 config would not be quietly skipped -- it would
    silently reshape that config. Ignoring it would be the ruling-6 violation;
    refusing it is the only way the author learns.

    Written so the *only* thing wrong with this config is its version: the role
    exists, the patch is legal, and no other `node_roles` validator has anything
    to say. Matched on the message, because a bare `ValidationError` here would
    pass just as well if one of the other two fired instead.
    """
    cfg = _cfg(_node("cov_3g", "indicator_latent"))
    cfg["version"] = 3
    cfg["node_roles"] = {"indicator_latent": {"unique": True}}

    with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="requires `version: 4`"):
        GraphConfig.model_validate(cfg)
```

## 1155. test_redeclaring_a_built_in_role_patches_it_rather_than_replacing_it

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_b2_node_roles.py:285](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_b2_node_roles.py:285)

```python
def test_redeclaring_a_built_in_role_patches_it_rather_than_replacing_it() -> None:
    """Naming a shipped role in `node_roles` states a key, not a whole spec.

    Max, 2026-08-11: shadowing should not be refused -- "you can specify what you
    like and defaults do the rest, not that defaults preclude hand-specification."
    An earlier draft raised on any entry naming a built-in. Two things were wrong
    with that beyond the taste question: it inverts the config's general shape, and
    it would make Q-B2c's "materialize early, delete late" unrepresentable for this
    key, since the block such a pass writes back names every built-in by
    definition.

    What this pins is the half that makes permitting it safe. If the base were a
    bare spec, stating one key would silently discard the four unstated ones --
    `indicator_latent` would keep `unique` and lose its demographic complement,
    which is the shipped-guarantee break the refusal was reaching for. Patching
    onto the same-named built-in is what removes the hazard rather than forbidding
    the case.
    """
    cfg = GraphConfig.model_validate(
        _cfg(
            _node("cov_3g", "indicator_latent"),
            node_roles={"indicator_latent": {"unique": True}},
        )
    )
    spec = cfg.resolved_node_roles()["indicator_latent"]

    assert spec.unique is True  # the stated key took effect
    assert spec.axes == "default_disagg"  # and the unstated ones survived
    assert spec.observable is True
```

```python
def test_two_nodes_may_not_claim_one_code() -> None:
    """A code identifies rows, so two claimants make the loader's filter ambiguous.

    Rejected at validation rather than at load: by the time the sheet is open, the
    only available repair is to guess which node the rows meant. `aka` colliding
    with another node's *primary* `indicator` is the sharpest form -- the collision
    is silent in a way two identical `indicator:` fields would not be.

    Landed as a `GraphConfig` validator rather than a desugar pass, so the config
    is built *inside* the `raises` block. While this was xfailing, that was the one
    thing to avoid: `ValidationError` is a `ValueError`, so `extra="forbid"`
    rejecting the unknown `aka:` key would have satisfied the assertion for
    entirely the wrong reason. With the field landed, `aka:` is a known key and the
    only `ValueError` mentioning `gdp_pc` is the collision itself.
    """
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="gdp_pc"):
        _config(
            [
                _beta_prior("gdp", indicator="gdp", aka=["gdp_pc"]),
                _beta_prior("gdp_per_capita", indicator="gdp_pc"),
            ]
        )
```

```python
def _config(nodes: list[dict], edges: list[dict] | None = None) -> GraphConfig:
    """A minimal v4 config around `nodes`, so each pin states only its own subject.

    `version: 4` is explicit here rather than defaulted, per the pin-audience rule:
    a test taking `LATEST_VERSION` silently re-aims itself at whatever ships next.
    """
    return GraphConfig.model_validate(
        {
            "version": 4,
            "axes": {"country": {"kind": "categorical", "levels": ["US", "GB"]}},
            "nodes": nodes,
            "edges": edges or [],
        }
    )
```

```python
def _beta_prior(node_id: str, **fields) -> dict:
    """A well-formed beta prior node, for pins whose subject is not the CPD.

    Several roles below are carried by constructors that demand real structure to
    validate (`transition_logits` wants drivers, `constraint_v0` wants bindings).
    Those pins declare `role:` outright on a trivially-valid CPD instead, so that a
    failure means "this role's code reached the filter" and not "this CPD was
    underspecified". Group 1's first pin still goes through a constructor's
    `default_role`, which is what keeps the registry itself covered.
    """
    return {
        "id": node_id,
        "cpd": {
            "family": "beta",
            "constructor": "prior",
            "hyperparameters": {"alpha": 1.0, "beta": 1.0, "axes": ["country"]},
        },
        **fields,
    }
```

```python
def _cfg() -> GraphConfig:
    """An observable latent that declares no code, and a child that names none.

    Neither node carries an `indicator:` field, which is the point: the two must
    come out on opposite sides of the filter, so the answer cannot be coming from
    the declaration. `effect_group.sum` is used for the child because its
    registered `default_role` is `effect_group_sum` -- a shipped role that names
    no sheet quantity and, unlike `observation`/`constraint_v0`, is **not**
    caught by the current prefix rule. That is what makes this pin fail today
    rather than pass by accident.
    """
    return GraphConfig.model_validate(
        {
            "version": 4,
            "axes": {"country": {"kind": "categorical", "levels": ["US", "GB"]}},
            "nodes": [
                {
                    "id": "cov_3g",
                    "role": "indicator_latent",
                    "cpd": {
                        "family": "beta",
                        "constructor": "prior",
                        "hyperparameters": {
                            "alpha": 1.0, "beta": 1.0, "axes": ["country"],
                        },
                    },
                },
                {
                    "id": "coverage_total",
                    "cpd": {"family": "effect_group", "constructor": "sum"},
                },
            ],
            "edges": [{"parent": "cov_3g", "child": "coverage_total"}],
        }
    )
```

```python
def _inheriting(parent_nodes: list[dict], child_id: str = "cov_obs") -> GraphConfig:

    child = {
```

```python
def _resolved(cfg: GraphConfig, node_id: str) -> str | None:
    """The `indicator` desugar wrote onto `node_id`.

    The two pins below assert here rather than on `declared_indicator_codes`,
    because for an *observation* node the filter cannot see the answer: the prefix
    rule drops any `observation*` role regardless of what it resolved to, so a
    node-id fallback and a correct inheritance are indistinguishable downstream.
    Asserting the resolved field states the subject directly -- and it keeps
    stating it after B3 removes the prefix rule.
    """
    return {node.id: node.indicator for node in cfg.nodes}[node_id]
```

## 1179. test_the_priors_root_ambient_is_writable_at_the_top_level

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_b4_autoconstruct_priors_root.py:92](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_b4_autoconstruct_priors_root.py:92)

```python
def test_the_priors_root_ambient_is_writable_at_the_top_level() -> None:
    """The authoring surface, and it is tri-state.

    ``None`` and ``False`` must stay distinguishable: the general ``autoconstruct``
    key is what an unset specific key falls back to, so collapsing unset into
    ``False`` would make the fallback unobservable and the quantifier pointless.
    Contrast the general key, which bottoms the family out and so defaults to a
    plain ``True`` (``test_v4_autoconstruct_flag.py``).

    The two *writes* come first deliberately. Reading the field off a config that does
    not set it raises ``AttributeError`` today, not ``ValidationError`` -- so leading
    with the unset case made this pin xfail for a reason unrelated to the field's
    absence from the schema, and it failed outright against the marker. Writing first
    puts the authoring surface, which is what B4 owes, in front of the tri-state
    detail that only matters once the field exists.
    """
    assert _anchor_cfg(version=4, autoconstruct_priors=False).autoconstruct_priors is False
    assert _anchor_cfg(version=4, autoconstruct_priors=True).autoconstruct_priors is True
    assert _anchor_cfg(version=4).autoconstruct_priors is None
```

## 1184. test_an_emitted_prior_carries_its_consumers_obs_answer

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_b4_autoconstruct_priors_root.py:165](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_b4_autoconstruct_priors_root.py:165)

```python
def test_an_emitted_prior_carries_its_consumers_obs_answer() -> None:
    """B6's detachment stamp, pinned here because the priors walk is B4's.

    A ``priors.<role>`` block lives inside its consumer and inherits that consumer's
    autoconstruct answers, not the top level's (Max, 2026-08-14). The *priors* answer is
    already threaded down the walk's worklist -- the same inheritance by another means --
    but the *obs* answer is not, and an emitted prior is a node D1 will have to answer
    about too. So the walk stamps ``autoconstruct_obs`` at the moment it detaches the
    block. Read between passes, since ``strip_autoconstruct_flags`` removes it by the end.

    The consumer says ``false`` while the global stays at its ``true`` default, so a
    stamp taken from the wrong scope reads ``true`` and fails here. Full rationale for
    stamping only nested nodes: ``test_b6_autoconstruct_obs.py``'s header.
    """
    config = _anchor_cfg(version=4)
    config = config.model_copy(
        update={
            "nodes": [
                node.model_copy(update={"autoconstruct_obs": False})
                if node.id == "seg_logits"
                else node
                for node in config.nodes
            ]
        }
    )
    for name, pass_fn in _passes_for(4):
        config = pass_fn(config)
        if name == "autoconstruct_priors":
            break
    emitted = [node for node in config.nodes if node.id not in _AUTHORED]
    assert {node.id for node in emitted} >= {"theta_weight", "theta_bias"}
    assert all(node.autoconstruct_obs is False for node in emitted)
```

```python
def test_desugar_strips_the_top_level_priors_flag() -> None:
    """Normalization, and it is what holds H10's keep-list at three names.

    A fully desugared config carries one top-level ``autoconstruct: false`` and no
    per-predicate key: by then no predicate has anything left to autoconstruct, so
    they cannot disagree in output. If ``autoconstruct_priors`` survived here,
    ``_H10_EXCEPTIONS`` would have to grow to admit it
    (``test_h10_ruling13_falsifier.py``), which is exactly the question this stamp
    answers. The cpd-level key is already stripped today

    rather than inventing one.

    out = desugar(_anchor_cfg(version=4, autoconstruct_priors=True))
```

## 1190. _names_marker_anywhere

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_b5_fork_a_routing.py:72](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_b5_fork_a_routing.py:72)

```python
def _names_marker_anywhere(raw: dict) -> bool:
    """Does the authored text name Fork-A, in any of its spellings?

    Deliberately a dumb recursive scan of the loaded YAML rather than a walk over
    typed nodes: the point is to be blind to *where* the marker sits, so that a
    config naming it somewhere the predicate has not been taught about still
    counts as naming it. That is what makes the sweep below a falsifier.
    """
    if isinstance(raw, dict):
        return any(_names_marker_anywhere(v) for v in raw.values())
    if isinstance(raw, list):
        return any(_names_marker_anywhere(v) for v in raw)
    return raw == FORK_A_MARKER
```

```python
@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", sorted(EXAMPLES.glob("*.yaml")), ids=lambda p: p.name)
def test_naming_fork_a_and_routing_to_it_agree(path: Path) -> None:
    """No shipped example may name Fork-A and be routed away from it.

    The failure B5 fixed was *silent*: a config whose nodes say ``observation_v0``
    while the router reports none is a contradiction nothing was watching for. This
    is the watcher, and it is a test rather than a runtime guard because reading the
    graph removes the way the two could disagree -- there is no longer a marker
    location for the reader to fall behind.
    """
    with open(path) as f:
        raw = YAML().load(f)
    config = GraphConfig.model_validate(raw)
    try:
        graph = build_graph(config, data_resolver=_stub_resolver)
    except ValueError as exc:
        # Not every example builds standalone, and one that does not has no route
        # to disagree about. Asserted by name rather than skipped on any failure,
        # so a *newly* unbuildable example fails here instead of quietly dropping
        # out of the sweep.
        assert path.name in UNBUILDABLE_STANDALONE, f"{path.name} stopped building: {exc}"
        pytest.skip(f"{path.name}: {UNBUILDABLE_STANDALONE[path.name]}")
    assert graph_has_observation_v0_sites(graph) is _names_marker_anywhere(raw)
```

## 1199. _desugar_through

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_b6_autoconstruct_obs.py:157](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_b6_autoconstruct_obs.py:157)

```python
def _desugar_through(config: GraphConfig, last_pass: str) -> GraphConfig:
    """Run desugar's passes in order, stopping after ``last_pass``.

    A detachment stamp is mid-desugar state -- the strip removes it -- so it needs a view
    between passes. ``test_pass_idempotence.py`` already drives the pass order this way;
    this is the prefix form of the same access, and it means claim 1 does not have to
    wait for C4's per-pass dump hook to become observable.

    ``KeyError`` when the pass does not exist, which was the expected failure while the
    (since withdrawn) ``resolve_autoconstruct_obs`` pass was unwritten.
    """
    passes = _passes_for(4)
    names = [name for name, _ in passes]
    if last_pass not in names:
        raise KeyError(f"{last_pass!r} is not a desugar pass; have {names}")
    for name, pass_fn in passes:
        config = pass_fn(config)
        if name == last_pass:
            return config
    raise AssertionError("unreachable: pass present but never reached")
```

```python
def test_a_flag_the_author_set_beats_the_ambient(node_flag: bool) -> None:
    """The near scope overrides; it is not merged with the far one.

    Both directions, so the rule is override and not merely ``and``/``or``: with the
    global at its ``true`` default, ``and`` would pass the ``False`` case and
    ``or`` the ``True`` case, so testing one direction would leave the readings
    indistinguishable.

    ``ValidationError`` and not the ``KeyError`` its sibling above predicted: writing
    the node flag is refused at validation, which happens before any resolution could
    be reached. The two failure modes sorted the pins cleanly -- a pin failed on the
    missing *field* iff it wrote one, and on the missing *pass* otherwise.
    """
    config = _cfg([_prior("cov_3g", autoconstruct_obs=node_flag)])
    assert _autoconstruct_obs_at(config.nodes[0], _root_ambient(config)) is node_flag
```

## 1205. test_scope_beats_specificity

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_b6_autoconstruct_obs.py:239](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_b6_autoconstruct_obs.py:239)

```python
def test_scope_beats_specificity() -> None:
    """The precedence rule, ruled 2026-08-14 (Max): **scope first, then specificity**.

    The two axes only conflict in one shape -- a *specific* key at a *distant* scope
    against a *general* key at a near one -- and this is that shape. The node's bare
    ``autoconstruct: true`` quantifies over every predicate at its scope, including
    obs; the top level names obs specifically and forbids it. The node wins.

    Chosen over specificity-first because it extends claim 1 (nearest encompassing)
    instead of adding a second, competing rule, and because it keeps the author's
    model one-dimensional: read the closest place something is said, then the most
    specific key said *there*. Specificity-first would mean a top-level line silently
    outranking a line written on the node itself, which is the opposite of what
    writing it on the node looks like it does.

    ``ValidationError``: neither the node's bare ``autoconstruct`` nor the top-level
    ``autoconstruct_obs`` was a field when this was pinned, so validation refused the
    config well before any precedence logic could run.
    """
    config = _cfg([_prior("cov_3g", autoconstruct=True)], autoconstruct_obs=False)
    assert _root_ambient(config) is False
    assert _autoconstruct_obs_at(config.nodes[0], _root_ambient(config)) is True
```

## 1206. test_a_detached_obs_node_carries_its_latents_answer

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

```python
def test_a_detached_obs_node_carries_its_latents_answer() -> None:
    """The one place a value *is* stamped, and the reason it has to be.

    An ``obs:`` entry inherits its latent's answer, not the top level's (Max,
    2026-08-14). Detaching it into a top-level node is exactly what puts that answer
    out of its reach, so ``expand_obs`` stamps it at the moment it detaches -- the
    latent says ``false`` here while the global stays at its ``true`` default, so a
    stamp taken from the wrong scope reads ``true`` and fails.
    """
    config = _cfg(
        [
            _prior(
                "cov_3g",
                autoconstruct_obs=False,
                obs=[{"source": "itu", "unit": "pct", "cpd": _OBS_CPD}],
            )
        ]
    )
    flat = _desugar_through(config, _DETACH_PASS)
    emitted = next(node for node in flat.nodes if node.id.endswith("__obs"))
    assert emitted.autoconstruct_obs is False
```

```python
def test_nothing_else_is_stamped() -> None:
    """The negative half, and the whole reason per-pass idempotence survives.

    Stamping every node was the original design and was withdrawn (Max, 2026-08-14):
    it "adds a new field to practically everything in the config, which doesn't
    correspond to anything in the graph". Only nodes that were nested carry a value, so
    once everything is detached the stamp has an empty *domain* rather than a no-op
    effect -- which is what makes each pass a fixed point on desugared output by
    construction. ``test_pass_idempotence.py`` is where that is enforced; this pins the
    property it rests on.
    """
    config = _cfg([_prior("cov_3g"), _prior("cov_4g")])
    flat = _desugar_through(config, _DETACH_PASS)
    assert all(node.autoconstruct_obs is None for node in flat.nodes)
```

## 1212. test_the_v3_baseline_dump_carries_no_empty_fields

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_b6_autoconstruct_obs.py:369](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_b6_autoconstruct_obs.py:369)

```python
def test_the_v3_baseline_dump_carries_no_empty_fields() -> None:
    """Why the flag family can grow without churning every ≤v3 baseline.

    ``canonical()`` is a bare ``model_dump(mode="json")``
    (``scripts/regen_v3_baseline.py``), so a new optional field lands in all fifteen
    desugar baselines as an explicit ``null`` and every phase that adds one
    regenerates the lot. The baseline's own docstring says "the diff is the finding";
    a diff that is mostly new nulls is a finding about nothing.

    Note what does *not* justify this: ``autoconstruct_obs`` is v4-only behavior, and
    these baselines are ≤v3 (Max, 2026-08-13). The churn comes from the field
    *existing* on a shared model, not from anything ≤v3 does with it.

    ``exclude_none`` rather than ``exclude_defaults``: the latter would also drop a
    field an author set *to* its default, which is information the baseline exists
    to hold.

    Pinned on the dump function rather than on the committed files, so it passes the
    moment the strategy changes and does not depend on when they are regenerated --
    which is why it needed no edit when the strategy did change, only its decorator
    removed. Green since 2026-08-13; a standing guard from here.

    Note what this does *not* check, because ``canonical`` still does not dump
    ``by_alias``: that the baseline text can be read back as a config. It cannot, and
    could not before pruning either -- see
    ``scratchpad/probe_canonical_not_roundtrippable.py``.
    """
    from digital_readiness.scripts import regen_v3_baseline as regen

    _, config = regen.load(regen.EXAMPLES / "demo_v0.yaml")
    assert "null" not in regen.canonical(regen.desugar(config))
```

```python
    the two are different answers: the block is deferred to D2 while the
    constructor inside it is defaulted here and now. So the guard compares

    deferred side.
```

## 1226. _loaded

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_bundled_aggregation.py:69](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_bundled_aggregation.py:69)

```python
def _loaded(*, family: str = "normal", site_id: str = "obs_normal") -> LoadedObservations:
    """One bundle: genderless income cells + gendered pop cells.

    Income is declared (so it's kept + bound); pop is undeclared here (it only
    feeds ``pop.weights_FM``), so ``_attach_observations`` gates it out. The
    family/site default to the identity-link ``normal`` bundle (which isolates
    the aggregation question); pass ``lognormal``/``obs_lognormal`` to exercise
    the demo's actual positive-valued family.
    """
    cells: list[dict] = []
    values: list[float] = []
    for c in COUNTRIES:
        cells.append(_cell("dispinc_pc", c))
        values.append(INCOME[c])
    for c in COUNTRIES:
        for g in GENDERS:
            cells.append(_cell("pop", c, gender=g))
            values.append(POP[(c, g)])
    bundle = ObservationCellBundle(
        site_id=site_id,
        family=family,
        cells=tuple(cells),
        values=jnp.asarray(values, dtype=jnp.float32),
    )
    n = len(cells)
    return LoadedObservations(cell_bundles=(bundle,), n_rows_read=n, n_rows_kept=n)
```

## 1230. test_bundled_path_reproduces_gender_aggregation

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_bundled_aggregation.py:165](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_bundled_aggregation.py:165)

```python
def test_bundled_path_reproduces_gender_aggregation(_registry) -> None:
    """The bundled obs reproduces the demo's per-capita mean over gender.

    Identity link => the traced obs location IS the gender-collapsed latent mean,
    so we compare it to a hand-computed population-weighted mean. This is the
    payoff of deriving selector keys from the latent's axes
    (``observations/_common.py::_axis_pins``): the genderless income cell pins
    ``country`` + ``year`` by value-membership and reduces the unpinned
    ``gender`` axis via ``per_capita`` -- no literal ``geo_finest`` key.
    """
    loaded = _loaded()
    with pytest.warns(UserWarning, match="pop"):
        graph = build_graph(
            _config(), loaded, data_resolver=make_observation_resolver(loaded)
        )

    model = compile_model(graph)
    with numpyro.handlers.seed(rng_seed=0):
        with numpyro.handlers.trace() as tr:
            model()  # prior trace -- the obs loc is computed from the latent

    latent = np.asarray(tr["dispinc_pc"]["value"])  # (country, year, gender)
    pop = np.array(
        [[[POP[(c, g)] for g in GENDERS]] for c in COUNTRIES]
    )  # (country, year=1, gender)
    # population-weighted mean over gender, per (country, year) -- what the demo's
    # income_obs computes and what the bundled obs SHOULD reproduce per cell.
    expected = (latent * pop).sum(axis=2) / pop.sum(axis=2)  # (country, year)

    obs_loc = np.asarray(tr["obs_normal"]["fn"].loc)  # one entry per income cell
    assert obs_loc == pytest.approx(expected.reshape(-1), rel=1e-5)
```

## 1231. test_bundled_lognormal_matches_demo_likelihood

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_bundled_aggregation.py:203](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_bundled_aggregation.py:203)

```python
def test_bundled_lognormal_matches_demo_likelihood(_registry) -> None:
    """The bundled ``lognormal.observation`` reproduces the demo's likelihood.

    The demo wires income through ``lognormal.observation_v0`` (loc=log(level),
    scale=0.1) with ``aggregate_over=("gender",)``. The family-bundled node
    instead infers the gender collapse structurally, so it must land on the
    SAME likelihood per cell: ``LogNormal(log(weighted mean over gender), 0.1)``.
    We read loc/scale straight off the traced distribution and compare.
    """
    loaded = _loaded(family="lognormal", site_id="obs_lognormal")
    with pytest.warns(UserWarning, match="pop"):
        graph = build_graph(
            _config(), loaded, data_resolver=make_observation_resolver(loaded)
        )

    obs = graph.get("obs_lognormal")
    assert obs.cpd_spec.family == "lognormal"
    assert obs.cpd_spec.constructor == "observation"

    model = compile_model(graph)
    with numpyro.handlers.seed(rng_seed=0):
        with numpyro.handlers.trace() as tr:
            model()

    latent = np.asarray(tr["dispinc_pc"]["value"])  # (country, year, gender)
    pop = np.array([[[POP[(c, g)] for g in GENDERS]] for c in COUNTRIES])
    weighted_mean = (latent * pop).sum(axis=2) / pop.sum(axis=2)  # (country, year)

    fn = tr["obs_lognormal"]["fn"]
    # loc = log(median) where median is the population-weighted gender mean...
    assert np.asarray(fn.loc) == pytest.approx(
        np.log(weighted_mean).reshape(-1), rel=1e-5
    )
    # ...and the log-scale is the demo's sigma (kappa=100 => 1/sqrt(kappa)=0.1).
    assert np.asarray(fn.scale) == pytest.approx(DEMO_INCOME_SIGMA, rel=1e-6)
```

## 1232. _pop_loaded

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_bundled_aggregation.py:240](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_bundled_aggregation.py:240)

```python
def _pop_loaded() -> LoadedObservations:
    """One bundle of gendered population cells, with ``pop`` declared observable.

    Each cell pins every latent axis (country/year/gender), so it routes through
    the *atomic* read in ``_atomic_index`` -- the gendered-atomic path. Cells are
    spelled the config's way (``"F"``/``"M"``), which is what a real load now
    produces: ``LoaderSpec.canonical`` settles the spelling once, at the load.
    """
    cells: list[dict] = []
    values: list[float] = []
    for c in COUNTRIES:
        for g in GENDERS:
            cells.append(_cell("pop", c, gender=g))
            values.append(POP[(c, g)])
    bundle = ObservationCellBundle(
        site_id="obs_pop",
        family="lognormal",
        cells=tuple(cells),
        values=jnp.asarray(values, dtype=jnp.float32),
    )
    n = len(cells)
    return LoadedObservations(cell_bundles=(bundle,), n_rows_read=n, n_rows_kept=n)
```

```python
def test_bundled_gendered_atomic_population(_registry) -> None:
    """A gendered-atomic obs reads each cell elementwise across the case split.

    Population is observed per (country, gender): every cell pins all three
    latent axes, so the bundled obs should read the matching latent element
    directly -- no aggregation. On the log link the obs loc is therefore ``log``
    of the per-cell latent.
    """
    loaded = _pop_loaded()
    graph = build_graph(
        _pop_config(), loaded, data_resolver=make_observation_resolver(loaded)
    )

    obs = graph.get("obs_pop")
    assert obs.cpd_spec.family == "lognormal"
    assert set(graph.parents("obs_pop")) == {"pop"}

    model = compile_model(graph)
    with numpyro.handlers.seed(rng_seed=0):
        with numpyro.handlers.trace() as tr:
            model()

    latent = np.asarray(tr["pop"]["value"])  # (country, year, gender)
    # Cells are emitted (country, gender)-major matching _pop_loaded's loops.
    expected = np.array(
        [latent[ci, 0, gi] for ci in range(len(COUNTRIES)) for gi in range(len(GENDERS))]
    )
    fn = tr["obs_pop"]["fn"]
    assert np.asarray(fn.loc) == pytest.approx(np.log(expected), rel=1e-5)
```

## 1235. test_bundled_binds_by_node_id_without_extra_tag

```python
def test_bundled_binds_by_node_id_without_extra_tag(_registry) -> None:
    """A node whose id IS its data-sheet code needs no ``extra.indicator`` tag.

    The canonical convention: the indicator code is the node id, so
    ``node_id == IndicatorMeta.indicator == cell.indicator`` and both the
    build-time wiring (``build.py``) and the runtime lookup line up with no
    explicit tag. Dropping ``extra`` from the otherwise-identical pop config
    must still build, bind, and trace the obs node.
    """
    cfg = _pop_config().model_dump()
    cfg["nodes"][0].pop("extra", None)  # rely on node id == "pop"
    config = GraphConfig.model_validate(cfg)
    loaded = _pop_loaded()

    graph = build_graph(
        config, loaded, data_resolver=make_observation_resolver(loaded)
    )
    assert set(graph.parents("obs_pop")) == {"pop"}

    model = compile_model(graph)
    with numpyro.handlers.seed(rng_seed=0):
        with numpyro.handlers.trace() as tr:
            model()
    assert "obs_pop" in tr
```

```python
    name: str, cfg: GraphConfig, tmp_path: Path
) -> None:
    """Done-when: intermediate config emitted per example, and it reloads.

    A non-empty file is not enough -- stable serialization means the bytes
    load back as a ``GraphConfig``.
    """
    from digital_readiness.io.config.desugar import emit_intermediate_config

    flat = desugar(cfg)
    target = tmp_path / f"{name}.intermediate.yaml"
    emit_intermediate_config(flat, target)
    text = target.read_text()
    assert text.strip()
    reloaded = GraphConfig.model_validate(YAML().load(text))
    assert isinstance(reloaded, GraphConfig)
```

## 1256. test_intermediate_emission_uses_the_shared_serializer

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_c3_intermediate_config_emission.py:98](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_c3_intermediate_config_emission.py:98)

```python
@needs("C5", AttributeError)
def test_intermediate_emission_uses_the_shared_serializer(
    tmp_path: Path,
) -> None:
    """C3 and A1b share one serializer (C5); the dump must go through it.

    Pinned to C5, not C3, because the shared writer does not exist until then. Once
    both land, re-serializing the config must reproduce the file
    ``emit_intermediate_config`` wrote, byte for byte.

    The ``.serialize`` call comes **before** ``emit_intermediate_config`` on purpose.
    Both are absent today, so whichever runs first decides which step this pin
    reports -- and the step id has to be the one it is actually waiting on, or it
    will not clear when that lands. Under the previous free-function shape the
    ``serialize_config`` import happened to sort first and this ordering was free;
    with a method there is no import to sort, so the order is now load-bearing.
    """
    path = _EXAMPLES / "segmentation_child_v4.yaml"
    flat = desugar(GraphConfig.model_validate(YAML().load(path.read_text())))
    expected = flat.serialize("yaml")

    from digital_readiness.io.config.desugar import emit_intermediate_config

    target = tmp_path / "intermediate.yaml"
    emit_intermediate_config(flat, target)
    assert target.read_text() == expected
```

```python
def _example_configs() -> list[tuple[str, GraphConfig]]:
    out: list[tuple[str, GraphConfig]] = []
    for path in sorted(_EXAMPLES.glob("*.yaml")):
        cfg = GraphConfig.model_validate(YAML().load(path.read_text()))
        if cfg.version < 2:
            # v1 returns unchanged from desugar; the YAML round trip is still
            # meaningful, but the pass list is not what C5(a) is probing.
            continue
        out.append((path.name, cfg))
    return out
```

## 1269. test_format_is_required

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_c5_config_serializer.py:87](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_c5_config_serializer.py:87)

```python
@needs("C5", AttributeError)
def test_format_is_required() -> None:
    """``format`` has no default: see the module docstring.

    Pinned rather than left to review because a default is the kind of thing added
    later for convenience, and the convenience is exactly what this forbids.

    Two-layer on purpose. The marker is ``AttributeError`` -- the method's *absence*,
    which is what fails today -- while the missing default is checked by the inner
    ``pytest.raises(TypeError)``. Marking the whole thing ``TypeError`` was the first
    attempt and it was wrong: today's ``AttributeError`` would have satisfied it, so
    the pin could not tell "no method yet" from "method that took a default", which
    is the one distinction it exists to draw. Split this way, a C5 that ships a
    default raises nothing here and fails loudly instead of xpassing.
    """
    cfg = GraphConfig()
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        cfg.serialize()  # type: ignore[call-arg]
```

```python
def test_no_module_level_serializer() -> None:
    """Green, and green **before** C5 too -- deliberately.

    This asserts an *absence*, so it cannot be a pin: there is nothing for C5 to
    make it stop raising. Its job is to fail the day someone re-adds a free
    ``serialize_config`` as a thin shim over the method. That shim would satisfy
    the export pins these tests used to carry while putting two names on one
    concept, which is the sort of green-that-means-nothing the ``needs`` machinery
    exists to prevent.
    """
    assert not hasattr(config_pkg, "serialize_config")
    assert "serialize_config" not in config_pkg.__all__
```

```python
@needs("C5", AttributeError)
@pytest.mark.filterwarnings("ignore::UserWarning")
@pytest.mark.parametrize(("name", "cfg"), _EXAMPLE_CASES, ids=_IDS)
def test_desugar_yaml_load_desugar_is_byte_exact(
    name: str, cfg: GraphConfig
) -> None:
    """C5(a): serialize(desugar(cfg)) equals serialize(desugar(load(that)))."""
    flat = desugar(cfg)
    yaml1 = flat.serialize("yaml")
    reloaded = GraphConfig.model_validate(YAML().load(yaml1))
    yaml2 = desugar(reloaded).serialize("yaml")
    assert yaml1 == yaml2, f"byte-exact round trip failed for {name}"
```

```python
@needs("C5", AssertionError)
def test_a1b_regen_canonical_uses_the_shared_serializer() -> None:
    """A1b shares this serializer (Underspecified #4).

    Today ``regen_v3_baseline.canonical`` writes JSON by hand -- it picks the dump
    options and calls ``json.dumps`` itself. After C5 it must delegate to
    ``.serialize("json")`` so baseline regen and C3 emission cannot drift apart in
    the options they choose.

    Matching on ``.serialize(`` rather than on the bare word: ``serialize`` alone
    would also match a comment mentioning it, or the old free-function name, and
    this assertion is the only thing standing between "shares one path" and
    "happens to agree today".
    """
    import inspect

    from digital_readiness.scripts.regen_v3_baseline import canonical

    assert ".serialize(" in inspect.getsource(canonical)
```

```python
def test_gate_drops_undeclared_indicator_cells_and_warns() -> None:
    cfg = _v1({"nodes": [_beta_prior_node("cov_3g", indicator="cov_3g")]})
    declared = _cell("cov_3g", "KEN")
    undeclared = _cell("cov_4g", "KEN")  # cov_4g not declared in config
    bundle = _bundle("obs_beta", "beta", declared, undeclared)

    with pytest.warns(UserWarning, match="cov_4g"):
        graph = build_graph(cfg, _loaded(bundle))

    # only the declared cell survives into the obs node
    assert graph.get("obs_beta").cpd_spec.hyperparameters["cells"] == (declared,)
    # the undeclared indicator gets no node and no edge
    assert "cov_4g" not in graph
```

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

```python
def _sugar_config() -> GraphConfig:
    """The declared config with its obs node + edges stripped.

    This is the *sugar* form: the author writes only the latents and lets
    ``build_graph``'s auto-attach resynthesize the family-bundled obs node from
    the loaded data. Derived from ``DECLARED_OBS_YAML`` (rather than authored
    separately) so the two can't drift.
    """
    raw = YAML().load(DECLARED_OBS_YAML)
    raw["nodes"] = [n for n in raw["nodes"] if n["id"] != "obs_beta"]
    raw["edges"] = []
    return GraphConfig.model_validate(raw)
```

## 1311. test_explicit_obs_node_is_the_desugared_form_of_auto_attach

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_config_declared_obs.py:164](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_config_declared_obs.py:164)

```python
def test_explicit_obs_node_is_the_desugared_form_of_auto_attach(_registry) -> None:
    """The keystone reduction: the *sugar* (omit the obs node, let auto-attach
    synthesize it from loaded data) lands on the *same* obs node the explicit
    declaration spells out.

    This is the relationship the whole reference design rests on -- the explicit
    config is the desugared target, auto-attach is the sugar -- so it is asserted
    directly here by building both ways and comparing, rather than checking the
    explicit side alone. Hyperparameter *values* may differ (the explicit node
    overrode ``default_concentration``; the auto-attached node takes the family
    template default); the structural contract -- identity, kind, family,
    constructor, covered indicators, arity, and the latent edges -- is what the
    desugaring guarantees and what this pins.
    """
    explicit_g = build_graph(_config())
    loaded = _loaded()
    sugar_g = build_graph(
        _sugar_config(), loaded, data_resolver=make_observation_resolver(loaded)
    )

    explicit, sugar = explicit_g.get("obs_beta"), sugar_g.get("obs_beta")

    def covered(node) -> list[str]:
        cells = node.cpd_spec.hyperparameters["cells"]
        return sorted({str(c["indicator"]) for c in cells})

    assert (sugar.kind, sugar.cpd_spec.family, sugar.cpd_spec.constructor) == (
        explicit.kind,
        explicit.cpd_spec.family,
        explicit.cpd_spec.constructor,
    ) == ("observation", "beta", "observation")
    assert covered(sugar) == covered(explicit) == sorted(COV_INDICATORS)
    assert len(sugar.cpd_spec.hyperparameters["cells"]) == len(
        explicit.cpd_spec.hyperparameters["cells"]
    )
    assert set(sugar_g.parents("obs_beta")) == set(explicit_g.parents("obs_beta")) == set(
        COV_INDICATORS
    )
```

## 1314. _loaded

[tests/io/test_config_demo.py:63](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_config_demo.py:63)

```python
def _loaded(*extra_indicators: str) -> LoadedObservations:
    """One ``obs_beta`` bundle carrying every coverage indicator's cells.

    ``extra_indicators`` adds present-but-undeclared cells (one per geo, value
    0.5) to exercise the gate -- they are never declared in the config below.
    """
    cells: list[dict] = []
    values: list[float] = []
    for ind in COV_INDICATORS:
        for geo, val in zip(GEOS, COV_VALUES[ind]):
            cells.append(_cell(ind, geo))
            values.append(val)
    for ind in extra_indicators:
        for geo in GEOS:
            cells.append(_cell(ind, geo))
            values.append(0.5)
    bundle = ObservationCellBundle(
        site_id="obs_beta",
        family="beta",
        cells=tuple(cells),
        values=jnp.asarray(values, dtype=jnp.float32),
    )
    n = len(cells)
    return LoadedObservations(cell_bundles=(bundle,), n_rows_read=n, n_rows_kept=n)
```

```python
def _cov_prior_node(indicator: str) -> dict:
    # Mirrors the demo's coverage latent (_demo_assembly.py L484-494): a per-cell
    # Beta(1, 1) on (country, year), tagged with its observable indicator so the
    # family-bundled obs node can bind to it.
    return {
        "id": indicator,
        "kind": "prior",
        "extra": {"indicator": indicator},
        "cpd": {
            "family": "beta",
            "hyperparameters": {
                "alpha": 1.0,
                "beta": 1.0,
                "axes": ["country", "year"],
            },
        },
    }
```

```python
def _cov_standardize_node(indicator: str) -> dict:
    # Mirrors cov_*_z (_demo_assembly.py L511-538): identity-transform z-score
    # whose center/scale are panel-derived -- here carried as DataRefs that the
    # resolver materializes to the mean / ddof-0 sd of the loaded values.
    return {
        "id": f"{indicator}_z",
        "kind": "zscore",
        "cpd": {
            "family": "standardize",
            "hyperparameters": {
                "center": {
                    "from_data": "standardize.center",
                    "args": {"indicator": indicator, "transform": "identity"},
                },
                "scale": {
                    "from_data": "standardize.scale",
                    "args": {"indicator": indicator, "transform": "identity"},
                },
                "transform": "identity",
            },
        },
    }
```
