## 1325. test_undeclared_indicator_gated_out_end_to_end

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_config_demo.py:274](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_config_demo.py:274)

```python
def test_undeclared_indicator_gated_out_end_to_end(_registry) -> None:
    loaded = _loaded("ghost")  # a third indicator present in data, never declared
    with pytest.warns(UserWarning, match="ghost"):
        graph = build_graph(
            _demo_cov_config(), loaded, data_resolver=make_observation_resolver(loaded)
        )
    # the undeclared indicator earns no node and no obs cell
    assert "ghost" not in graph
    obs_cells = {str(c["indicator"]) for c in graph.get("obs_beta").cpd_spec.hyperparameters["cells"]}
    assert "ghost" not in obs_cells
    assert obs_cells == set(COV_INDICATORS)
    # ...and the gated graph still builds + compiles + traces. The build step
    # drops ghost from the obs NODE's cells; ``LoadedObservations.gated`` drops
    # the same cells from the runtime VALUE array, so the two line up and the
    # obs site's cell-axis length equals its value-array length. Feeding the
    # gated view (rather than the raw ``loaded``, whose values still carry the
    # ghost rows) is what makes the trace consistent without a length mismatch.
    gated = loaded.gated(COV_INDICATORS)
    model = compile_model(graph)
    with numpyro.handlers.seed(rng_seed=0):
        with numpyro.handlers.trace() as tr:
            model(observations=gated.to_observations())
    assert tr["obs_beta"]["is_observed"] is True
    # the gated value array matches the obs node's surviving cell count
    assert tr["obs_beta"]["value"].shape == (len(COV_INDICATORS) * len(GEOS),)
```

[tests/io/test_config_inferred_structure.py:90](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_config_inferred_structure.py:90)

```python
def _drop_structural_axes(raw: dict) -> dict:
    """Strip the inferable structural axes + add ``segment_count``.

    Removes the ``segment``/``transition``/``driver`` axis declarations and the
    redundant ``segment_levels`` on ``segment_shares`` (the continuation_ratio
    CPD self-synthesizes them), and sets ``segment_count: 4`` as the source of K.
    The disaggregation axes (country/year/gender) are left declared.
    """
    for axis in ("segment", "transition", "driver"):
        del raw["axes"][axis]
    raw["segment_count"] = 4
    for node in raw["nodes"]:
        if node["id"] == "segment_shares":
            node["cpd"]["hyperparameters"].pop("segment_levels", None)
    return raw
```

```python
def _drop_logit_bridge_priors(raw: dict) -> dict:
    """Strip ``theta_bias``/``theta_weight`` and their edges into ``seg_logits``."""
    theta_ids = {"theta_bias", "theta_weight"}
    raw["nodes"] = [n for n in raw["nodes"] if n["id"] not in theta_ids]
    raw["edges"] = [
        e for e in raw["edges"] if not (e[0] in theta_ids and e[1] == "seg_logits")
    ]
    return raw
```

## 1330. _drop_upstream_driver_pairs

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_config_inferred_structure.py:121](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_config_inferred_structure.py:121)

```python
def _drop_upstream_driver_pairs(raw: dict) -> dict:
    """Strip driver ``_z`` nodes + wiring; tag roots ``indicator_role: upstream``.

    Removes the standardizer nodes and the ``root -> _z`` / ``_z -> seg_logits``
    edges for the three demo upstream drivers, and tags each root so the build
    step synthesizes the missing chain. ``transform`` is carried on the root
    (``log`` for income, ``identity`` for coverage) -- the same values the
    explicit ``demo_v0.yaml`` standardizers declare.
    """
    z_ids = set(_UPSTREAM_Z)
    raw["nodes"] = [n for n in raw["nodes"] if n["id"] not in z_ids]
    raw["edges"] = [
        e
        for e in raw["edges"]
        if e[0] not in z_ids and not (e[1] in z_ids and e[0] in _UPSTREAM_DRIVERS)
    ]
    for node in raw["nodes"]:
        if node["id"] == "income":
            node.setdefault("extra", {})["indicator_role"] = "upstream"
            node["extra"]["transform"] = "log"
        elif node["id"] in ("cov_3g", "cov_4g"):
            node.setdefault("extra", {})["indicator_role"] = "upstream"
            node["extra"]["transform"] = "identity"
    return raw
```

## 1331. _drop_downstream_manifestation_pairs

```python
def _drop_downstream_manifestation_pairs(raw: dict) -> dict:
    """Strip mixture-mean nodes + parent wiring; keep mean->child edges.

    Removes the ``*_mean`` manifestation nodes and only the synthesizable
    parent edges (``segment_shares -> mean``, ``profile -> mean``). Edges from
    the mean to obs nodes and constraints stay declared so the sugar path can
    wire them once the mean is pre-synthesized at build time.
    """
    mean_ids = set(_DOWNSTREAM_MEANS)
    profile_ids = set(_DOWNSTREAM_PROFILES)
    raw["nodes"] = [n for n in raw["nodes"] if n["id"] not in mean_ids]
    raw["edges"] = [
        e
        for e in raw["edges"]
        if not (
            (e[0] == "segment_shares" and e[1] in mean_ids)
            or (e[0] in profile_ids and e[1] in mean_ids)
        )
    ]
    return raw
```

```python
def _tag_driver_sign(raw: dict, driver_id: str, sign: str, *, sign_loc: float | None = None) -> dict:
    node = next(n for n in raw["nodes"] if n["id"] == driver_id)
    node.setdefault("extra", {})["sign"] = sign
    if sign_loc is not None:
        node["extra"]["sign_loc"] = sign_loc
    return raw
```

## 1334. _weight_loc_by_driver

```python
def _weight_loc_by_driver(built) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Read the synthesized per-driver ``theta_weight`` location (gender/t avg)."""
    import jax.numpy as jnp

    axes = built.get("theta_weight").cpd_spec.hyperparameters["axes"]
    driver_axis = next(a for a in axes if a.name == "driver")
    loc = jnp.asarray(built.get("theta_weight").cpd_spec.hyperparameters["loc"])
    return {
        driver: float(jnp.mean(loc[:, :, idx]))
        for idx, driver in enumerate(driver_axis.levels)
    }
```

```python
def test_structural_axes_are_droppable() -> None:
    """Dropping segment/transition/driver (+ segment_levels) infers them back.

    The inferred levels are read off the resolved ``axes`` on the declared nodes
    that reference them: ``theta_*`` carry transition/driver, ``profile_*`` carry
    segment. Inference reproduces the demo's ``t1..t3`` / ``income,cov_3g,cov_4g``
    / ``S1..S4``.
    """
    panel = _panel()
    loaded = _loaded_from_panel(panel)
    built = build_graph(
        _config(_drop_structural_axes(_demo_raw())),
        data_resolver=make_observation_resolver(loaded),
    )

    def axes_of(node_id: str) -> dict[str, tuple]:
        return {
            a.name: a.levels
            for a in built.get(node_id).cpd_spec.hyperparameters["axes"]
        }

    bias_axes = axes_of("theta_bias")
    assert bias_axes["transition"] == ("t1", "t2", "t3")  # T = K - 1 = 3
    weight_axes = axes_of("theta_weight")
    assert weight_axes["driver"] == ("income", "cov_3g", "cov_4g")  # wired order
    profile_axes = axes_of("profile_mobinet")
    assert profile_axes["segment"] == ("S1", "S2", "S3", "S4")  # K = 4
```

## 1339. test_logit_bridge_priors_are_the_desugared_form

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_config_inferred_structure.py:263](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_config_inferred_structure.py:263)

```python
def test_logit_bridge_priors_are_the_desugared_form() -> None:
    """Omitting ``theta_bias``/``theta_weight`` synthesizes the same nodes.

    Mirrors ``test_explicit_obs_node_is_the_desugared_form_of_auto_attach``:
    build the explicit demo and the theta-stripped sugar, and assert the synth
    nodes match the explicit ones on identity, ``(kind, family, constructor)``,
    role tag, resolved axes, and the edge into ``seg_logits``. (Values may differ;
    structure is the contract.)
    """
    panel = _panel()
    loaded = _loaded_from_panel(panel)
    resolver = make_observation_resolver(loaded)

    explicit = build_graph(_config(_demo_raw()), data_resolver=resolver)
    sugar = build_graph(
        _config(_drop_logit_bridge_priors(_demo_raw())), data_resolver=resolver
    )

    for node_id, role in (("theta_bias", "biases"), ("theta_weight", "weights")):
        e, s = explicit.get(node_id), sugar.get(node_id)
        assert (s.kind, s.cpd_spec.family, s.cpd_spec.constructor) == (
            e.kind,
            e.cpd_spec.family,
            e.cpd_spec.constructor,
        ) == ("prior_v0", "normal", None)
        assert s.extra.get("logit_role") == e.extra.get("logit_role") == role
        # resolved axes equal the explicit node's (name + levels + kind)
        sa = [(a.name, a.levels, a.kind) for a in s.cpd_spec.hyperparameters["axes"]]
        ea = [(a.name, a.levels, a.kind) for a in e.cpd_spec.hyperparameters["axes"]]
        assert sa == ea
        # edge into the anchor present in both
        assert "seg_logits" in sugar.children(node_id)
        assert "seg_logits" in explicit.children(node_id)
```

```python
def test_stripped_sign_example_builds(_registry) -> None:
    """The shipped ``demo_v0_stripped_sign.yaml`` example parses, desugars, and runs.

    Guards the authoring example against drift: structural axes, theta priors,
    driver standardizers, and manifestation means are omitted; ``sign`` tags on
    upstream drivers steer the synthesized ``theta_weight``.
    """
    panel = _panel()
    loaded = _loaded_from_panel(panel)
    with open(STRIPPED_SIGN_YAML) as f:
        cfg = GraphConfig.model_validate(YAML().load(f))

    built = build_graph(cfg, data_resolver=make_observation_resolver(loaded))
    reference = demo.demo_graph(panel)

    assert _signature(built) == _signature(reference)
    assert _edges(built) == _edges(reference)

    locs = _weight_loc_by_driver(built)
    assert locs["income"] == pytest.approx(1.0)
    assert locs["cov_3g"] == pytest.approx(1.0)
    assert locs["cov_4g"] == pytest.approx(1.0)  # sign: positive, default magnitude

    model = compile_model(built)
    result = run_map(model, built, demo.demo_observations(panel), steps=25, seed=0)
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(result.losses))
```

```python
def test_upstream_driver_pair_is_the_desugared_form() -> None:
    """Omitting ``_z`` + wiring for upstream drivers synthesizes the same nodes.

    Keystone for increment 4.2: build the explicit demo and the driver-stripped
    sugar (roots tagged ``indicator_role: upstream``) and assert each synthesized
    ``_z`` matches the explicit standardizer on identity, family, transform, and
    resolved center/scale, plus the edges into ``seg_logits``.
    """
    panel = _panel()
    loaded = _loaded_from_panel(panel)
    resolver = make_observation_resolver(loaded)

    explicit = build_graph(_config(_demo_raw()), data_resolver=resolver)
    sugar = build_graph(
        _config(_drop_upstream_driver_pairs(_demo_raw())), data_resolver=resolver
    )

    for z_id, transform, data_ind in (
        ("income_z", "log", "dispinc_pc"),
        ("cov_3g_z", "identity", "cov_3g"),
        ("cov_4g_z", "identity", "cov_4g"),
    ):
        e, s = explicit.get(z_id), sugar.get(z_id)
        assert (s.kind, s.cpd_spec.family, s.cpd_spec.constructor) == (
            e.kind,
            e.cpd_spec.family,
            e.cpd_spec.constructor,
        ) == ("zscore", "standardize", None)
        assert s.cpd_spec.hyperparameters["transform"] == transform
        assert s.cpd_spec.hyperparameters["center"] == e.cpd_spec.hyperparameters["center"]
        assert s.cpd_spec.hyperparameters["scale"] == e.cpd_spec.hyperparameters["scale"]
        root_id = z_id[:-2]  # strip "_z"
        assert root_id in sugar.parents(z_id)
        assert "seg_logits" in sugar.children(z_id)
        assert explicit.children(z_id) == sugar.children(z_id) == ("seg_logits",)
        # income binds standardize constants to dispinc_pc, not the node id
        if data_ind == "dispinc_pc":
            assert root_id == "income"
```

```python
def test_all_downstream_profiles_desugar_to_reference() -> None:
    """Each downstream profile, stripped individually, still matches the reference."""
    panel = _panel()
    loaded = _loaded_from_panel(panel)
    resolver = make_observation_resolver(loaded)
    explicit = build_graph(_config(_demo_raw()), data_resolver=resolver)

    for mean_id, profile_id in zip(_DOWNSTREAM_MEANS, _DOWNSTREAM_PROFILES):
        raw = _demo_raw()
        raw["nodes"] = [n for n in raw["nodes"] if n["id"] != mean_id]
        raw["edges"] = [
            e
            for e in raw["edges"]
            if not (
                (e[0] == "segment_shares" and e[1] == mean_id)
                or (e[0] == profile_id and e[1] == mean_id)
            )
        ]
        sugar = build_graph(_config(raw), data_resolver=resolver)
        e, s = explicit.get(mean_id), sugar.get(mean_id)
        assert (s.kind, s.cpd_spec.family) == (e.kind, e.cpd_spec.family)
        assert sugar.parents(mean_id) == ("segment_shares", profile_id)
```

```python
def test_declared_manifestation_suppresses_synthesis() -> None:
    """Declaring ``mobinet_mean`` produces no duplicate; ``smartphone_mean`` synths."""
    panel = _panel()
    loaded = _loaded_from_panel(panel)
    raw = _drop_downstream_manifestation_pairs(_demo_raw())
    explicit_mean = next(
        n for n in YAML().load(open(DEMO_YAML))["nodes"] if n["id"] == "mobinet_mean"
    )
    raw["nodes"].append(copy.deepcopy(explicit_mean))
    raw["edges"].extend(
        [["segment_shares", "mobinet_mean"], ["profile_mobinet", "mobinet_mean"]]
    )
    built = build_graph(_config(raw), data_resolver=make_observation_resolver(loaded))

    assert "mobinet_mean" in built and "smartphone_mean" in built
    assert built.get("mobinet_mean").cpd_spec.family == "manifestation"
    assert built.get("smartphone_mean").cpd_spec.family == "manifestation"
    assert built.parents("mobinet_mean") == ("segment_shares", "profile_mobinet")
    assert built.parents("smartphone_mean") == ("segment_shares", "profile_smartphone")
```

```python
def test_maximally_desugared_including_drivers_lands_on_reference(_registry) -> None:
    """Strip structural axes, theta priors, driver pairs, AND manifestation means."""
    panel = _panel()
    loaded = _loaded_from_panel(panel)
    raw = _drop_downstream_manifestation_pairs(
        _drop_upstream_driver_pairs(
            _drop_logit_bridge_priors(_drop_structural_axes(_demo_raw()))
        )
    )
    built = build_graph(_config(raw), data_resolver=make_observation_resolver(loaded))
    reference = demo.demo_graph(panel)

    assert _signature(built) == _signature(reference)
    assert _edges(built) == _edges(reference)

    model = compile_model(built)
    result = run_map(model, built, demo.demo_observations(panel), steps=25, seed=0)
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(result.losses))
    shares = result.posterior["segment_shares"].isel(chain=0, draw=0).values
    np.testing.assert_allclose(shares.sum(axis=-1), 1.0, atol=1e-5)
```

## 1355. test_declared_structural_axis_is_not_overwritten

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_config_inferred_structure.py:615](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_config_inferred_structure.py:615)

```python
def test_declared_structural_axis_is_not_overwritten() -> None:
    """Declaring ``transition`` explicitly leaves its levels untouched.

    Drop only segment/driver (keep transition declared, with a non-default level
    set) + add segment_count. The declared transition wins; segment/driver still
    infer. Proves inference is absence-triggered per axis.
    """
    panel = _panel()
    loaded = _loaded_from_panel(panel)
    raw = _demo_raw()
    del raw["axes"]["segment"]
    del raw["axes"]["driver"]
    raw["segment_count"] = 4
    for node in raw["nodes"]:
        if node["id"] == "segment_shares":
            node["cpd"]["hyperparameters"].pop("segment_levels", None)
    # the declared transition axis is left as-is (t1..t3)
    built = build_graph(_config(raw), data_resolver=make_observation_resolver(loaded))
    trans = next(
        a
        for a in built.get("theta_bias").cpd_spec.hyperparameters["axes"]
        if a.name == "transition"
    )
    assert trans.levels == ("t1", "t2", "t3")  # the declared value, untouched
```

```python
def test_declared_theta_prior_suppresses_synthesis() -> None:
    """Declaring ``theta_bias`` produces no duplicate; ``theta_weight`` still synths.

    Strip only ``theta_weight`` (+ its edge); ``theta_bias`` stays declared. The
    bias role is filled by the declaration, so only the weight is synthesized.
    """
    panel = _panel()
    loaded = _loaded_from_panel(panel)
    raw = _demo_raw()
    raw["nodes"] = [n for n in raw["nodes"] if n["id"] != "theta_weight"]
    raw["edges"] = [
        e for e in raw["edges"] if not (e[0] == "theta_weight" and e[1] == "seg_logits")
    ]
    built = build_graph(_config(raw), data_resolver=make_observation_resolver(loaded))

    # exactly one theta_bias (the declared one), one theta_weight (synthesized)
    assert "theta_bias" in built and "theta_weight" in built
    assert built.get("theta_weight").extra.get("logit_role") == "weights"
    assert "seg_logits" in built.children("theta_weight")
    assert "seg_logits" in built.children("theta_bias")
```

```python
def _cfg(role: str) -> GraphConfig:
    """One node, a member role, an indicator no sheet mentions, no ``obs:``."""
    return GraphConfig.model_validate(
        {
            "version": 4,
            "axes": {"country": {"kind": "categorical", "levels": ["US", "GB"]}},
            "nodes": [
                {
                    "id": "lonely",
                    "indicator": "no_such_indicator_in_any_sheet",
                    "role": role,
                    "cpd": {
                        "family": "beta",
```

```python
@pytest.mark.parametrize("role", sorted(COMPLEMENT_ROLES))
def test_a_member_role_with_no_data_gets_no_children(role: str) -> None:
    """Desugar invents no observation for a member role it has no data for.

    Parametrized over the whole set rather than over ``segment`` alone: the
    B2 unification says membership is uniform, so the invariant has to hold for
    every member or the set really did need a carve-out.
    """
    cfg = desugar(_cfg(role))

    assert [(e.parent, e.child) for e in cfg.edges] == []

    # And the role survived, so the parametrization is testing what it claims:
    # a node whose role desugar dropped would pass this vacuously.
    (node,) = cfg.nodes
    assert resolve_role(node) == role
```

## 1388. _sheet

[tests/io/test_d1_autoconstruct_obs_entries.py:70](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_d1_autoconstruct_obs_entries.py:70)

```python
def _sheet(*triples: tuple[str, str, str]) -> LoadedObservations:
    """Loaded observations carrying exactly ``(code, source, unit)`` rows.

    Built through the frame constructor [15:34] rather than by hand: cells and
    bundles are downstream of autoconstruction -- bundle ids are desugar's to
    assign [12:47] -- so a fixture that pre-assembles them would ask these pins to
    read the wrong thing.

    One row per triple, all on ``USA``: the claims here are about which *entries*
    appear, and a second country would multiply the rows without changing that.
    """
    frame = pd.DataFrame(
        [
            {
                "indicator_code": code,
                "source_code": source,
                "unit": unit,
                "country_iso3": "USA",
                "year": 2020,
                "value": 0.5,
                # The default filter keeps actuals only, and naming an absent
                # column is an error [10:39], so the column has to be here.
                "obs_status": "A",
            }
            for code, source, unit in triples
        ]
    )
    return load_observations_from_frame(frame)
```

```python
def _entry_keys(node) -> set[tuple[str, str]]:
    """``obs`` is ``None`` until populated; read that as no entries.

    So an unpopulated node fails these pins on the set they assert, not on a
    helper iterating ``None``.
    """
    return {(entry.source, entry.unit) for entry in node.obs or ()}
```

## 1394. test_entries_sharing_a_distribution_land_in_one_bundle

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_d1_autoconstruct_obs_entries.py:170](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_d1_autoconstruct_obs_entries.py:170)

```python
@needs("D1", AssertionError)
def test_entries_sharing_a_distribution_land_in_one_bundle() -> None:
    """Claim 6, in the registry's own terms.

    Max: "This should be available from the CPD registry. I believe similar bundling
    logic is already implemented for priors." It is, and the field is
    ``ConstructorEntry.distribution`` (``core/cpd.py``) -- required iff the
    constructor is bundlable, and the thing bundle members must *agree* on, which is
    what already makes cross-family bundling refusable by comparing declared names.
    So "assigned by their stated sample function" is assignment keyed on the declared
    distribution.

    But the mechanism exists on the prior layer only. ``distribution`` is declared
    today by exactly two constructors, ``normal.prior_v0`` and
    ``lognormal.prior_v0``; every observation constructor hardcodes its class inside
    ``fn`` and declares nothing, so the registry currently answers ``None`` for the
    layer this pin is about. D1 therefore has a prerequisite the pin does not state
    in code: the obs constructors must declare their distributions. That is a
    three-line change per family (Beta, Normal, LogNormal are all plain classes) --
    but it is not nothing, and ``normal.truncated`` shows the general rule has a
    known hole, since a distribution *factory* cannot be declared at all
    (``core/cpd.py``, ``DistributionClass``).
    """
    sheet = _sheet(("cov_3g", "itu", "pct"), ("cov_3g", "gsma", "pct"))
    flat = desugar(_cfg([_prior("cov_3g")]), sheet)
    obs_nodes = [n for n in flat.nodes if n.id.startswith("cov_3g") and n.id != "cov_3g"]
    bundle_ids = {n.bundle_id for n in obs_nodes}
    assert len(obs_nodes) == 2
    assert len(bundle_ids) == 1 and None not in bundle_ids
```

```python
@needs("D1", ValueError)
def test_two_authored_entries_claiming_one_pair_is_refused() -> None:
    """Claim 7's contradiction half: "an error if there's a contradiction that makes
    it impossible to know how to fill in the rest."

    Two entries claiming one ``(source, unit)`` with *different* CPDs is the
    contradiction that cannot be resolved by filling: neither is more specific, so
    there is no rule that picks. Refused at desugar, where both are visible, rather
    than at compile time where only the survivor would be.

    The overlap here is exact rather than pattern-vs-exact deliberately -- a pattern
    overlapping a more specific entry has an obvious reading (the specific one wins)
    and is a separate question, not yet ruled on.
    """
    one = {"source": "itu", "unit": "pct", "cpd": {"family": "beta"}}
    two = {"source": "itu", "unit": "pct", "cpd": {"family": "normal"}}
    sheet = _sheet(("cov_3g", "itu", "pct"))
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="itu"):
        desugar(_cfg([_prior("cov_3g", obs=[one, two])]), sheet)
```

## 1405. test_the_observation_edge_comes_from_the_latent_not_an_inheriting_obs_node

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_d1_indicator_gate.py:137](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_d1_indicator_gate.py:137)

```python
def test_the_observation_edge_comes_from_the_latent_not_an_inheriting_obs_node() -> None:
    """The direction hazard: an obs node conditions on a latent, never on an obs node.

    ``income`` and an inheriting obs node both resolve to ``dispinc_pc``
    (``_INDICATOR_INHERITING_ROLES``), so a gate keyed on the resolved indicator is
    many-to-one with last-write-wins. If the inheritor won, the edge would run
    obs-to-obs — a cycle in the intended dependency direction, silent and far from
    its cause. ``_observable_latents`` has to skip the inheritors.

    The config here writes an ``obs:`` block naming no ``source`` or ``unit``, which
    on the data path is the maximal template: its payload lands on the observation
    the sheet holds rather than becoming a second node reading the same row. So
    ``income_obs`` is absorbed, and the assertion is that what remains hangs off the
    latent.
    """
    graph = build_graph(_cfg(with_obs_block=True), _loaded(_row("dispinc_pc", "KEN")))

    assert graph.children("income") == (_OBS,), (
        "the observation is conditioned on an inheriting obs node rather than on "
        "the latent, or the keyless `obs:` block became a second reading of the "
        "same row instead of settings for the one the data holds"
    )
    assert "income_obs" not in graph
    # The template was consumed, not dropped: its payload reached the derived node.
    hypers = graph.get(_OBS).cpd_spec.hyperparameters
    assert hypers["concentration"] == 50.0
```

## 1437. test_levels_resolved_from_data_constrain_the_grid_like_declared_ones

```python
def test_levels_resolved_from_data_constrain_the_grid_like_declared_ones() -> None:
    """[10:46] An axis whose membership comes from the data still has one.

    So the intersection is taken against the resolved list rather than the axis
    being waved through -- which here keeps both countries, because the resolver
    reads the same rows the grid does.

    Loaded with the config's own axis names (``loader_spec_from_config``, as
    ``io/pipeline.py`` does), because otherwise a row labels its geography
    ``geo_finest`` and this config's ``country`` axis meets nothing to constrain.
    """
    axes = {
        "country": {
            "kind": "categorical",
            "levels": {"from_data": "country.levels"},
        },
        "year": _AXES["year"],
    }
    cfg = _cfg([_latent("cov_3g")], axes=axes)
    loaded = load_observations_from_frame(
        pd.DataFrame(
            [
                _row("cov_3g", "itu", "pct", geo="KEN"),
                _row("cov_3g", "itu", "pct", geo="TZA"),
            ]
        ),
        spec=loader_spec_from_config(cfg),
    )
    flat = _quiet(cfg, loaded)
    assert sorted(_grid_axes(flat, "cov_3g__itu__pct__obs")["country"]) == [
        "KEN",
        "TZA",
    ]
```

```python
def _gendered(row: dict, level: str) -> dict:
    """``row`` as a gender-disaggregated row; the plain ``_row`` is the total.

    ``level`` is the sheet's code, ``"M"`` or ``"F"``, which the spec casefolds to the
    ``"m"``/``"f"`` levels the configs here declare. A code the spec does not know
    passes through as itself and is dropped by the level intersection.
    """
    return row | {"gender": level}
```

## 1439. _ungated

```python
def _ungated(*rows: dict) -> LoadedObservations:
    """Load with no totals gate, so gender slices reach the store.

    The loader's default ``axis_breakdown`` already holds gender at totals for every
    indicator but ``pop``, which is the older half of the same policy. These pins are
    about what desugar does when a slice *does* arrive, so they turn that gate off
    rather than relying on it.
    """
    return load_observations_from_frame(
        pd.DataFrame(list(rows)),
        spec=_SPEC,
        flt=ObservationLoadFilter(axis_breakdown={}),
    )
```

```python
def test_an_axis_the_config_does_not_declare_is_omitted_from_the_grid() -> None:
    """[08-24 10:52] The config never mentions gender, so the grid has no gender.

    Nothing is summed: the total is a row the sheet already carries, so dropping the

    case where every level is unrecognized.
```

## 1441. test_a_disaggregated_row_does_not_land_on_the_total_it_is_a_slice_of

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_d1_populate_obs_pass.py:566](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_d1_populate_obs_pass.py:566)

```python
def test_a_disaggregated_row_does_not_land_on_the_total_it_is_a_slice_of() -> None:
    """The reason omitting the axis is not enough on its own.

    Dropping `gender` from the grid's axes would leave the gendered rows in play, each
    landing on the total's coordinate and racing it. Here the total says 0.5 and the
    slices say 0.9; naming `gender` in ``at_total`` is what makes the grid report the
    total. Leaving it unnamed means "do not consult gender", which is a different
    request and the store's default -- see ``test_e1_observation_store.py``.
    """
    loaded = _ungated(
        _row("cov_3g", "itu", "pct"),
        _gendered(_row("cov_3g", "itu", "pct"), "F") | {"value": 0.9},
        _gendered(_row("cov_3g", "itu", "pct"), "M") | {"value": 0.9},
    )
    grid = loaded.grid(
        ("cov_3g", "itu", "pct"),
        {"year": [2020], "country": ["KEN"]},
        at_total=["gender"],
    )
    # `pct` arrives on the unit interval: 0.5 in the sheet is 0.005 here.
    assert float(grid.values[0, 0]) == pytest.approx(0.005)
    assert bool(grid.mask[0, 0])
```

```python
@needs("D3", ValidationError)
def test_incomplete_entry_is_filled_and_the_map_is_gone() -> None:

    Today fails at the B1 required-``cpd`` rule (``ValidationError``). When D2

    assert emitted.cpd is not None

    assert _MAP_KEY not in _dump_keys(flat)
    assert getattr(flat, _MAP_KEY, None) is None
```

```python
def _census_triples() -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
    """Distinct ``(indicator, source, unit)`` from the national-long census sheet."""
    df = pd.read_excel(
        _CENSUS_SHEET,
        usecols=["indicator_code", "source_code", "unit"],
    )
    rows = (
        df.drop_duplicates()
        .assign(
            indicator_code=lambda d: d["indicator_code"].astype(str),
            source_code=lambda d: d["source_code"].astype(str),
            unit=lambda d: d["unit"].astype(str),
        )
        .sort_values(["indicator_code", "source_code", "unit"])
    )
    return list(
        rows.itertuples(index=False, name=None)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    )
```

## 1485. test_merge_obs_entries_hand_fields_win

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

```python
@needs("D5", ImportError)
def test_merge_obs_entries_hand_fields_win() -> None:
    """Unit-level pin of the merge rule, independent of the full with-data path.

    Provisional: ``merge_obs_entries(auto, hand)`` -> hand values overlay auto
    on matching ``(source, unit)``; non-matching auto entries pass through.
    """
    from digital_readiness.io.config.desugar import merge_obs_entries
    from digital_readiness.io.config.schema import ObsEntryDef

    auto = [
        ObsEntryDef.model_validate(
            {
                "source": "itu",
                "unit": "pct",
                "cpd": {
                    "family": "beta",
                    "constructor": "observation_v0",
                    "hyperparameters": {"concentration": 50.0},
                },
            }
        ),
        ObsEntryDef.model_validate(
            {
                "source": "gsma",
                "unit": "pct",
                "cpd": {
                    "family": "beta",
                    "constructor": "observation_v0",
                    "hyperparameters": {"concentration": 50.0},
                },
            }
        ),
    ]
    hand = [
        ObsEntryDef.model_validate(
            {
                "source": "itu",
                "unit": "pct",
                "cpd": {
                    "family": "beta",
                    "constructor": "observation_v0",
                    "hyperparameters": {"concentration": 999.0},
                },
            }
        )
    ]
    merged = merge_obs_entries(auto, hand)
    by_pair = {(e.source, e.unit): e for e in merged}
    assert set(by_pair) == {("itu", "pct"), ("gsma", "pct")}
    assert by_pair[("itu", "pct")].cpd.hyperparameters["concentration"] == pytest.approx(
        999.0
    )
    assert by_pair[("gsma", "pct")].cpd.hyperparameters["concentration"] == pytest.approx(
        50.0
    )
```

```python
def _grid(node_id: str, *, axes: list[str]) -> dict:
    """A grid as `populate_obs` leaves one: identity axes, then the level axes.

    Written out rather than loaded, because grids only exist on the data path and
    what this pass reads is the shape, not the rows.
    """
    return {
        "id": node_id,
        "cpd": {
            "family": "beta",
            "constructor": "observation_grid",
            "hyperparameters": {
                "indicator": "x",
                "source": "S",
                "unit": "pct",
                "axes": {
                    "indicator": ["x"],
                    "source": ["S"],
                    "unit": ["pct"],
                    **{name: ["a"] for name in axes},
                },
                "at_total": [],
            },
        },
    }
```

## 1489. _cfg

```python
def _cfg(*nodes: dict, edges: list[list[str]], node_roles: dict | None = None) -> GraphConfig:
    payload: dict = {
        "version": 4,
        "axes": {
            "country": {"kind": "categorical", "levels": ["US", "GB"]},
            "gender": {"kind": "categorical", "levels": ["F", "M"]},
        },
        "nodes": [
            {
                "id": "population",
                "indicator": "pop",
                "role": "population",
                "cpd": {
                    "family": "lognormal",
                    # `lognormal` registers `prior_v0`, not `prior`; `beta`
                    # registers both. Not interchangeable.
                    "constructor": "prior_v0",
                    "hyperparameters": {
                        "mu": 0.0, "sigma": 1.0, "axes": ["country", "gender"],
                    },
                },
            },
            *nodes,
        ],
        "edges": [{"parent": p, "child": c} for p, c in edges],
    }
    if node_roles is not None:
        payload["node_roles"] = node_roles
    return GraphConfig.model_validate(payload)
```

## 1495. test_a_hand_written_pointer_is_left_alone

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_d6_population_edges.py:171](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_d6_population_edges.py:171)

```python
def test_a_hand_written_pointer_is_left_alone() -> None:
    """An author-written `population` pointer survives desugar untouched.

    Ported from the pointer-filling version of this file, and load-bearing now in a
    way it was not then: with the auto-fill gone, a hand-written pointer is the
    *only* way a cell-route latent gets weights, and h1's four nodes write theirs
    by hand. If some pass ever starts rewriting the key, those four go quiet.
    """
    cfg = _cfg(
        _latent("cov_3g", family="rate", axes=["country"]),
        edges=[],
    )
    latent = next(n for n in cfg.nodes if n.id == "cov_3g")
    assert latent.cpd is not None
    hp = dict(latent.cpd.hyperparameters)
    hp["population"] = {DATA_REF_KEY: "pop.weights_FM", "args": {"indicator": "hand_written"}}
    nodes = [
        n.model_copy(update={"cpd": n.cpd.model_copy(update={"hyperparameters": hp})})
        if n.id == "cov_3g"
        else n
        for n in cfg.nodes
    ]
    out = desugar(cfg.model_copy(update={"nodes": nodes}))
    pointer = next(n for n in out.nodes if n.id == "cov_3g").cpd.hyperparameters["population"]
    assert "hand_written" in repr(pointer)
```

```python
def test_two_roles_carrying_the_special_is_refused() -> None:
    """Which node the weights come from must have one answer.

    Declaring a role *adds to* the shipped registry, so a config naming its own
    population role leaves the built-in one carrying the special too. `special: []`
    on the built-in is how the special moves rather than duplicates.
    """
    cfg = _cfg(
        _latent("folks", family=None, axes=["country"], role="headcount"),
        edges=[],
        node_roles={
            "headcount": {"instance_of": "indicator_latent", "special": ["population"]},
        },
    )
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="more than one node"):
        desugar(cfg)
```

```python
def test_standardize_log_transform_uses_log_scale() -> None:
    # The income case: the constant is the mean/sd of log(values), and the same
    # number the income root `loc` references (root loc == standardize.center/log).
    vals = [100.0, 1000.0, 10000.0]
    loaded = _loaded(
        _bundle(
            "obs_normal",
            "normal",
            [_cell("income", g) for g in ("AAA", "BBB", "CCC")],
            vals,
        )
    )
    resolve = make_observation_resolver(loaded)

    log_center = resolve(_ref("standardize.center", indicator="income", transform="log"))
    id_center = resolve(_ref("standardize.center", indicator="income", transform="identity"))

    assert log_center == pytest.approx(float(np.mean(np.log(vals))))
    assert log_center != pytest.approx(id_center)  # log scale genuinely differs
```

```python
def test_pop_weights_returns_structured_array_with_contract() -> None:
    # Two countries x one year x two genders; counts pivot onto (country, year,
    # gender) and the return is a materialized StructuredArray, not a bare array.
    cells = [
        _cell("pop", "AAA", gender="F"),
        _cell("pop", "AAA", gender="M"),
        _cell("pop", "BBB", gender="F"),
        _cell("pop", "BBB", gender="M"),
    ]
    vals = [10.0, 11.0, 20.0, 21.0]
    loaded = _loaded(_bundle("obs_normal", "normal", cells, vals))
    resolve = make_observation_resolver(loaded)

    sa = resolve(_ref("pop.weights_FM"))

    assert isinstance(sa, StructuredArray)
    assert sa.array.shape == (2, 1, 2)  # (country, year, gender)
    assert tuple(a.name for a in sa.axes) == ("country", "year", "gender")
    assert sa.axes[0].levels == ("AAA", "BBB")
    # Straight from the selectors: the load already spelled them the config's way,
    # so nothing here re-cases them.
    assert sa.axes[2].levels == ("F", "M")
    assert sa.indicator == IndicatorMeta(indicator="pop", family="count", unit="people")
    assert sa.population is None
    # values land in the right (country, gender) cells
    assert float(sa.array[0, 0, 0]) == pytest.approx(10.0)  # AAA / F
    assert float(sa.array[1, 0, 1]) == pytest.approx(21.0)  # BBB / M
```

## 1514. test_dataref_config_builds_and_compiles_through_seam

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_data_binding.py:256](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_data_binding.py:256)

```python
def test_dataref_config_builds_and_compiles_through_seam(_registry) -> None:
    # A DataRef-bearing config: a lognormal income root whose `loc` is a
    # standardize.center/log ref, shaped on a `country` axis whose levels are a
    # country.levels ref. Built with the real resolver, it must (a) resolve to the
    # hand-computed values and (b) compile + trace.
    #
    # Pinned to ``version: 1``, the tier current when this landed (2026-06-22,
    # before the version gate existed). DataRef resolution is not version-gated, so
    # the pin does not narrow the subject -- it stops the assertion being silently
    # re-aimed at each new tier, which is how two <=v3 pins in ``test_pipeline.py``
    # had drifted to v4 unnoticed until B3 broke them (2026-08-12).
    vals = [100.0, 1000.0, 10000.0]
    geos = ("AAA", "BBB", "CCC")
    loaded = _loaded(
        _bundle("obs_normal", "normal", [_cell("income", g) for g in geos], vals)
    )
    cfg = GraphConfig.model_validate(
        {
            "version": 1,
            "axes": {
                "country": {
                    "levels": {"from_data": "country.levels"},
                    "kind": "categorical",
                }
            },
            "nodes": [
                {
                    "id": "income",
                    "kind": "prior_v0",
                    "cpd": {
                        "family": "lognormal",
                        "constructor": "prior_v0",
                        "hyperparameters": {
                            "loc": {
                                "from_data": "standardize.center",
                                "args": {"indicator": "income", "transform": "log"},
                            },
                            "scale": 1.0,
                            "axes": ["country"],
                        },
                    },
                }
            ],
        }
    )

    resolve = make_observation_resolver(loaded)
    graph = build_graph(cfg, data_resolver=resolve)

    spec = graph.get("income").cpd_spec
    assert spec.hyperparameters["loc"] == pytest.approx(float(np.mean(np.log(vals))))
    assert spec.hyperparameters["axes"][0].levels == geos

    model = compile_model(graph)
    with numpyro.handlers.seed(rng_seed=0):
        with numpyro.handlers.trace() as tr:
            model()
    assert tr["income"]["value"].shape == (len(geos),)
```

```python
def test_reference_graph_runs_map(_registry, panel: demo.Panel, loaded, config) -> None:
    built = build_graph(config, data_resolver=make_observation_resolver(loaded))
    model = compile_model(built)
    result = run_map(model, built, demo.demo_observations(panel), steps=25, seed=0)
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(result.losses))
    post = result.posterior
    assert set(post.data_vars) >= {"income", "population", "segment_shares"}
    income = post["income"].isel(chain=0, draw=0).values
    assert income.shape == (panel.n_countries, 1, panel.n_genders)
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(income)) and np.all(income > 0)
    shares = post["segment_shares"].isel(chain=0, draw=0).values
    np.testing.assert_allclose(shares.sum(axis=-1), 1.0, atol=1e-5)
```

```python
def _panel() -> demo.Panel:
    """A tiny 2-country x F/M cross-section -- enough to exercise every shape.

    Genderless arrays (income, coverage) are 1-D over country; gendered arrays
    (population, the manifestations) are 2-D over (country, gender). The frozen
    standardization constants follow ``load_panel``: log-scale for income,
    identity for coverage, ddof=0.
    """
    income = np.array([1000.0, 2000.0])
    cov_3g = np.array([0.5, 0.7])
    cov_4g = np.array([0.3, 0.6])
    log_income = np.log(income)
    return demo.Panel(
        countries=("AAA", "BBB"),
        genders=("F", "M"),
        income=income,
        cov_3g=cov_3g,
        cov_4g=cov_4g,
        mobinet=np.array([[0.4, 0.5], [0.6, 0.7]]),
        smartphone=np.array([[0.5, 0.6], [0.7, 0.8]]),
        population=np.array([[1.0e6, 1.1e6], [2.0e6, 2.1e6]]),
        income_center=float(log_income.mean()),
        income_scale=float(log_income.std()),
        cov_3g_center=float(cov_3g.mean()),
        cov_3g_scale=float(cov_3g.std()),
        cov_4g_center=float(cov_4g.mean()),
        cov_4g_scale=float(cov_4g.std()),
    )
```

## 1528. _loaded_from_panel

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_demo_reference.py:114](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_demo_reference.py:114)

```python
def _loaded_from_panel(panel: demo.Panel) -> LoadedObservations:
    """Adapter standing in for the (deferred) loader: panel -> LoadedObservations.

    Emits the cells the resolver vocabulary reads -- ``dispinc_pc`` (genderless),
    ``pop`` (gendered F/M), and the two coverage indicators (genderless) -- with
    selectors shaped exactly as the loader produces them (gender spelled the
    config's way, ``F``/``M``, which is what the load settles on). The
    resolver computes ``standardize.center/scale``, ``country.levels`` and
    ``pop.weights_FM`` from these, so the YAML's ``{from_data: ...}`` markers
    materialize to the same constants ``demo_graph`` froze from ``panel``.
    """
    def cell(indicator: str, ci: int, *, gender: str | None = None) -> dict:
        country = panel.countries[ci]
        selectors: dict = {"year": demo.YEAR, "geo_finest": country}
        if gender is not None:
            selectors["gender"] = gender
        return {
            "indicator": indicator,
            "source": "DEMO",
            "year": demo.YEAR,
            "unit": (country,),
            "selectors": selectors,
        }

    income_cells, income_vals = [], []
    cov3_cells, cov3_vals = [], []
    cov4_cells, cov4_vals = [], []
    pop_cells, pop_vals = [], []
    for ci in range(panel.n_countries):
        income_cells.append(cell("dispinc_pc", ci))
        income_vals.append(float(panel.income[ci]))
        cov3_cells.append(cell("cov_3g", ci))
        cov3_vals.append(float(panel.cov_3g[ci]))
        cov4_cells.append(cell("cov_4g", ci))
        cov4_vals.append(float(panel.cov_4g[ci]))
        for gi, g in enumerate(panel.genders):
            pop_cells.append(cell("pop", ci, gender=g))
            pop_vals.append(float(panel.population[ci, gi]))

    import jax.numpy as jnp

    bundles = (
        ObservationCellBundle("obs_income", "lognormal", tuple(income_cells), jnp.asarray(income_vals)),
        ObservationCellBundle("obs_pop", "lognormal", tuple(pop_cells), jnp.asarray(pop_vals)),
        ObservationCellBundle("obs_cov3", "beta", tuple(cov3_cells), jnp.asarray(cov3_vals)),
        ObservationCellBundle("obs_cov4", "beta", tuple(cov4_cells), jnp.asarray(cov4_vals)),
    )
    n = sum(len(b.cells) for b in bundles)
    return LoadedObservations(cell_bundles=bundles, n_rows_read=n, n_rows_kept=n)
```

## 1531. _signature

```python
def _signature(graph) -> dict[str, tuple]:
    """node_id -> (kind, family, constructor) -- the per-node structural fingerprint."""
    sig = {}
    for meta in graph.nodes():
        spec = meta.cpd_spec
        sig[meta.node_id] = (
            meta.kind,
            None if spec is None else spec.family,
            None if spec is None else spec.constructor,
        )
    return sig
```

## 1537. test_reference_graph_runs_map

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_demo_reference.py:234](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_demo_reference.py:234)

```python
def test_reference_graph_runs_map(_registry) -> None:
    """The YAML-built model is not just constructible but *runnable*.

    ``compile_model`` only builds the model callable; the CPDs are first
    *executed* during the MAP fit's SVI trace. That gap is where list-valued
    hyperparameters from the config path (e.g. ``profile_*``'s per-element
    ``a``/``b``, ``theta_*``'s ``loc``/``scale``) used to reach ``jnp.broadcast_to``
    untyped and crash -- the demo's hand-assembly pre-wraps them in ``jnp.asarray``
    but the YAML path does not. This conditions on the demo evidence and runs a
    handful of SVI steps so that execution path stays covered. Few steps, loose
    bar: structural runnability, not convergence.
    """
    panel = _panel()
    loaded = _loaded_from_panel(panel)
    built = build_graph(_config(), data_resolver=make_observation_resolver(loaded))
    model = compile_model(built)

    result = run_map(model, built, demo.demo_observations(panel), steps=25, seed=0)

    assert np.all(np.isfinite(result.losses))
    post = result.posterior
    # the latents the fit must surface, with their declared cell shapes.
    assert set(post.data_vars) >= {"income", "population", "segment_shares"}
    income = post["income"].isel(chain=0, draw=0).values
    assert income.shape == (panel.n_countries, 1, panel.n_genders)
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(income)) and np.all(income > 0)
    # segment_shares is a simplex over the segment axis -> each row sums to 1.
    shares = post["segment_shares"].isel(chain=0, draw=0).values
    np.testing.assert_allclose(shares.sum(axis=-1), 1.0, atol=1e-5)
```

## 1540. _loaded_from_panel

```python
def _loaded_from_panel(panel: demo.Panel) -> LoadedObservations:
    """Panel -> ``LoadedObservations`` for the resolver vocabulary only.

    Bundles use data-sheet indicator codes (``dispinc_pc``, ``pop``, …); they
    feed ``make_observation_resolver`` for ``{from_data: ...}`` markers but do
    **not** fill the declared obs nodes' ``cells``.
    """

    def cell(indicator: str, ci: int, *, gender: str | None = None) -> dict:
        country = panel.countries[ci]
        selectors: dict = {"year": demo.YEAR, "geo_finest": country}
        if gender is not None:
            selectors["gender"] = gender
        return {
            "indicator": indicator,
            "source": "DEMO",
            "year": demo.YEAR,
            "unit": (country,),
            "selectors": selectors,
        }

    income_cells, income_vals = [], []
    cov3_cells, cov3_vals = [], []
    cov4_cells, cov4_vals = [], []
    pop_cells, pop_vals = [], []
    for ci in range(panel.n_countries):
        income_cells.append(cell("dispinc_pc", ci))
        income_vals.append(float(panel.income[ci]))
        cov3_cells.append(cell("cov_3g", ci))
        cov3_vals.append(float(panel.cov_3g[ci]))
        cov4_cells.append(cell("cov_4g", ci))
        cov4_vals.append(float(panel.cov_4g[ci]))
        for gi, g in enumerate(panel.genders):
            pop_cells.append(cell("pop", ci, gender=g))
            pop_vals.append(float(panel.population[ci, gi]))

    bundles = (
        ObservationCellBundle(
            "obs_income", "lognormal", tuple(income_cells), jnp.asarray(income_vals)
        ),
        ObservationCellBundle("obs_pop", "lognormal", tuple(pop_cells), jnp.asarray(pop_vals)),
        ObservationCellBundle("obs_cov3", "beta", tuple(cov3_cells), jnp.asarray(cov3_vals)),
        ObservationCellBundle("obs_cov4", "beta", tuple(cov4_cells), jnp.asarray(cov4_vals)),
    )
    n = sum(len(b.cells) for b in bundles)
    return LoadedObservations(cell_bundles=bundles, n_rows_read=n, n_rows_kept=n)
```

```python
def _signature(graph, *, skip: frozenset[str]) -> dict[str, tuple]:
    sig = {}
    for meta in graph.nodes():
        if meta.node_id in skip:
            continue
        spec = meta.cpd_spec
        sig[meta.node_id] = (
            meta.kind,
            None if spec is None else spec.family,
            None if spec is None else spec.constructor,
        )
    return sig
```

```python
def _edges(graph, *, skip: frozenset[str]) -> set[tuple[str, str]]:
    return {
        (parent, child)
        for meta in graph.nodes()
        for child in graph.children(meta.node_id)
        if (parent := meta.node_id) not in skip and child not in skip
    }
```

```python
def _clip_fractions(a: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    eps = demo._OBS_FRACTION_EPS
    return np.clip(a, eps, 1.0 - eps)
```

## 1546. _bundled_observations

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_demo_reference_bundled.py:191](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_demo_reference_bundled.py:191)

```python
def _bundled_observations(panel: demo.Panel) -> Observations:
    """Evidence for the bundled graph: bundle literals + a constraint fill.

    ``obs_lognormal`` values follow declared cell order (income per country,
    then population per country x gender). ``obs_beta`` follows cov_3g then
    cov_4g per country. Constraints are observed at 0 like ``demo_observations``.
    """
    lognormal_vals: list[float] = []
    for ci in range(panel.n_countries):
        lognormal_vals.append(float(panel.income[ci]))
    for ci in range(panel.n_countries):
        for gi in range(panel.n_genders):
            lognormal_vals.append(float(panel.population[ci, gi]))

    beta_vals: list[float] = []
    for ci in range(panel.n_countries):
        beta_vals.append(float(_clip_fractions(panel.cov_3g)[ci]))
    for ci in range(panel.n_countries):
        beta_vals.append(float(_clip_fractions(panel.cov_4g)[ci]))

    # The constraint sites are taken from the demo graph by *name* only. Before
    # A2 this harvested demo's zero arrays and reused them here, which quietly
    # assumed the bundled graph's constraint cells have the same shape as the
    # unbundled demo's -- true today, but nothing enforced it, and bundling is
    # exactly the axis along which shapes move. A fill cannot make that mistake:
    # each site's shape is resolved against *this* graph at conditioning time.
    constraint_sites = {
        site
        for site in demo.demo_observations(panel).observed_sites()
        if site.startswith("constraint")
    }

    return Observations(
        rules=(
            fill(constraint_sites, 0.0),
            literal("obs_lognormal", jnp.asarray(lognormal_vals)),
            literal("obs_beta", jnp.asarray(beta_vals)),
        )
    )
```

```python
def _grid() -> StructuredArray:
    """A two-country, two-year observation grid with its identity axes.

    Deliberately built the long way rather than through a helper, because the
    helper that should build it is what ``observation_grid_axes`` pins below.
    ``indicator`` / ``source`` / ``unit`` are length 1 here, which is the whole
    convention: they are axes, not a separate header.
    """
    return StructuredArray(
        array=jnp.array([[[[[0.1, 0.2], [0.3, 0.4]]]]]),
        axes=(
            AxisMeta(name="indicator", levels=("cov_3g",), kind="categorical"),
            AxisMeta(name="source", levels=("itu",), kind="categorical"),
            AxisMeta(name="unit", levels=("pct",), kind="categorical"),
            AxisMeta(name="geo_finest", levels=("US", "GB"), kind="categorical"),
            AxisMeta(name="year", levels=(2020, 2021), kind="ordinal"),
        ),
        indicator=IndicatorMeta(indicator="cov_3g", family="rate", unit="pct"),
        population=None,
    )
```

```python
@needs("E1", AttributeError)
def test_addressing_an_unobserved_level_is_an_error_not_a_zero() -> None:
    """Levels are filtered to the observed ones, so an absent level is absent.

    The grid holds a level iff something is observed at it. Asking for a level
    that was filtered out must say so, rather than returning the value the
    masked slot happens to carry -- that value is fill, and reading it as
    evidence is exactly the fabrication ``Literal.value_for`` guards against on
    the shape side.

    Two halves, expressed separately because ``@needs`` can only pin today's
    failure: the *pin* is ``AttributeError`` (no ``select`` yet), and the
    ``pytest.raises`` is the post-E1 requirement -- once ``select`` exists this
    passes only if the absent level is a ``ValueError``, which is what the
    existing resolver already raises for a level not on an axis. So the pin says
    "unbuilt" and the body says "and when built, loud".
    """
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        _grid().select(geo_finest="FR")
```

```python
@needs("E1", ImportError)
def test_observation_grid_axes_keeps_only_observed_levels() -> None:
    """An axis holds a level iff some value is observed at it.
```

## 1560. test_observation_grid_axes_takes_its_axis_set_from_its_caller

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_e1_grid_addressed_observations.py:213](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_e1_grid_addressed_observations.py:213)

```python
@needs("E1", ImportError)
def test_observation_grid_axes_takes_its_axis_set_from_its_caller() -> None:
    """The axis set is *declared*, not hardcoded -- and not inferred here either.

    Two things this pin deliberately separates, because only one of them is
    settled:

    * **Settled, and pinned:** ``observation_grid_axes`` holds no vocabulary of
      its own. It carries whatever axes it is handed, so no sheet's axis set
      becomes the grid's ceiling. Names nobody has ever enumerated must work.
    * **Not settled, and deliberately not pinned:** *where* the declaration comes
      from, and how axis names are matched to spreadsheet column headers. The
      config's axis registry and a node's ``axes`` / ``include_axes`` clearly have
      a role (``io/config/schema.py``), but the mechanism is open, and it is D's
      to settle rather than something this pin should presume.

    So the axis set arrives as an argument, and ``observed`` only decides which
    *levels* within it survive.
    """
    from digital_readiness.core.observation_cell import observation_grid_axes

    axes = observation_grid_axes(
        indicator="cov_3g",
        source="itu",
        unit="pct",
        axes=("admin2", "quarter", "handset_tier"),
        observed=(
            {"admin2": "GB-SCT", "quarter": "2021Q1", "handset_tier": "low"},
            {"admin2": "GB-WLS", "quarter": "2021Q2", "handset_tier": "low"},
        ),
    )
    by_name = {ax.name: ax for ax in axes}
    assert set(by_name) == {
        "indicator",
        "source",
        "unit",
        "admin2",
        "quarter",
        "handset_tier",
    }
    # Declared, so carried; observed once, so length 1 -- the same first-class
    # length-1 axis the identity triple gets.
    assert by_name["handset_tier"].levels == ("low",)
```

```python
def test_observation_cell_has_no_identity_accessor() -> None:
    """Green, and load-bearing: ruling 12's tuple key is *not* being added.

    Rev. 9's E1 text still describes ``ObservationCell.identity``, so this is
    the test that stops it coming back. The grid replaced the need for it; a
    cell identity re-added now would be a second namespace beside the axes,
    which is the exact thing E1 exists to prevent.
    """
    assert not hasattr(ObservationCell, "identity")
    assert "identity" not in {f.name for f in fields(ObservationCell)}
```

```python
def test_an_unmapped_unit_reaches_the_store_but_makes_no_bundle(
    data_path: Path,
) -> None:
    """``_UNIT_TO_CELL_BUNDLE`` picks a *family*, which only the cell reading needs.

    So a unit it does not map is no longer dropped on the floor: it is surveyable
    and griddable, while cell bundling keeps its own skip-and-count. Choosing a
    family for it is D2's.
    """
    unmapped = "hours_per_week"
    assert unmapped not in _UNIT_TO_CELL_BUNDLE, "pick a unit the map really lacks"
    frame = pd.DataFrame(
        [
            {
                "indicator_code": "screen_time",
                "source_code": "SRC",
                "country_iso3": "KEN",
                "year": 2020,
                "unit": unmapped,
                "value": 12.5,
                "obs_status": "A",
            }
        ]
    )
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        out = loaded_from_frame(frame)
    assert len(out.records) == 1
    assert out.records[0].value == pytest.approx(12.5)
    assert out.cell_bundles == ()
    assert out.n_rows_skipped_unsupported_unit == 1
```

```python
def test_two_units_for_one_source_are_two_rows_not_a_repeat() -> None:
    """De-duplication keys on the whole row, so a second unit is not a repeat.

    H3's case. The earlier key omitted ``unit``, which made these two rows one row.

    The cell reading still collapses them, because ``_row_to_cell`` drops the
    measurement unit and so cannot tell the two cells apart. That is the store's
    reason to exist: what the cell paradigm cannot represent, it no longer decides.
    """
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        out = loaded_from_frame(pd.DataFrame([_row("pct"), _row("per 100 people")]))
    assert {r.unit for r in out.records} == {"pct", "per 100 people"}
```

```python
def test_a_grid_has_the_requested_shape_in_the_requested_order(loaded) -> None:
    """The caller's shape wins; the store has no order of its own.

    Monitoring, in the 11:50 sense, only in that it names two axes in an order --
    the point being pinned is that *the request* decides it, so a different request
    giving a different order is the behavior, not a failure.
    """
    survey = loaded.survey()
    triple = survey.triples[0]
    request = {"year": [2019, 2020], "geo_finest": ["KEN", "NGA"]}
    grid = loaded.grid(triple, request)
    assert grid.values.shape == (2, 2)
    assert grid.mask.shape == (2, 2)
    flipped = loaded.grid(triple, {"geo_finest": ["KEN", "NGA"], "year": [2019, 2020]})
    assert flipped.values.shape == (2, 2)
    assert float(flipped.values[0, 0]) == pytest.approx(float(grid.values[0, 0]))
```

```python
def test_a_grid_over_coarse_and_fine_rows_builds_without_error(loaded) -> None:
    """The store holds both without contradiction.

    A row asserting fewer axes than the request lands at the levels it does assert
    and nowhere else -- no broadcast, no guess. What to do about the coarse rows is
    the requester's question, asked where the node's axes are known.
    """
    frame = pd.DataFrame(

                "gender": "F",

                "indicator_code": "pct_smartphone",

                "unit": "pct",
                "value": 50.0,
                "obs_status": "A",
                "gender": "T",
            },

    )

        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")

        out = loaded_from_frame(frame, flt=ObservationLoadFilter(axis_breakdown={}))
    triple = ("pct_smartphone", "SRC", "pct")
    grid = out.grid(triple, {"gender": ["f", "m"]})
    assert grid.values.shape == (2,)
    assert bool(grid.mask[0]) and not bool(grid.mask[1])
```

## 1609. _masked_spec

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_e2_grid_membership_and_mask.py:88](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_e2_grid_membership_and_mask.py:88)

```python
def _masked_spec(mask, obs, *, levels=("US", "GB"), family=dist.Beta):
    """A one-axis spec carrying evidence and a mask alongside its parameters.

    Every mask pin below builds through here, so they all fail at the same
    place until ``SiteSpec`` grows the two fields -- which is what makes
    ``TypeError`` the honest prediction rather than a guess about which
    downstream call would break first.
    """
    from digital_readiness.core.structured_array import AxisMeta, IndicatorMeta

    n = len(levels)
    return SiteSpec(
        build=lambda **kw: family(**kw),
        params={
            "concentration1": jnp.full((n,), 2.0),
            "concentration0": jnp.full((n,), 2.0),
        },
        axes=(AxisMeta(name="geo_finest", levels=levels, kind="categorical"),),
        indicator=IndicatorMeta(indicator="cov_3g", family="rate", unit="pct"),
        obs=obs,
        mask=mask,
    )
```

## 1616. test_mask_and_obs_scatter_on_the_same_layout_as_the_parameters

```python
@needs("E2", TypeError)
def test_mask_and_obs_scatter_on_the_same_layout_as_the_parameters() -> None:
    """One layout, so a member cannot read back another member's mask.

    ``bundle_layout`` is already the single source of truth for who owns which
    flat slot; the mask joining it is what makes that guarantee cover evidence
    too, rather than only parameters.
    """
    from digital_readiness.core.site_spec import bundle_layout
    from digital_readiness.model.cpds.site_realization import scatter_params

    a = _masked_spec(
        mask=jnp.array([True, False]), obs=jnp.array([0.4, 0.0]), levels=("US", "GB")
    )
    b = _masked_spec(mask=jnp.array([True]), obs=jnp.array([0.7]), levels=("FR",))
    layout = bundle_layout((a, b))
    flat = scatter_params((a, b))
    assert layout == ((0, 2), (2, 1))
    assert flat["mask"].tolist() == [True, False, True]
```

## 1617. test_a_masked_slot_contributes_exactly_zero_log_density

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_e2_grid_membership_and_mask.py:203](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_e2_grid_membership_and_mask.py:203)

```python
@needs("E2", TypeError)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("family", [dist.Beta, dist.LogNormal])
def test_a_masked_slot_contributes_exactly_zero_log_density(family) -> None:
    """Family-independent, which product-with-zero is not.

    The fill value in the masked slot is deliberately outside each family's
    support -- 0.0 is not in ``Beta``'s open ``(0,1)`` nor in ``LogNormal``'s
    ``(0, inf)``. If masking works, the fill is never evaluated and the total is
    exactly the one-slot total. If it were conditioned instead, this is ``-inf``.
    """
    kw = (
        {"concentration1": 2.0, "concentration0": 2.0}
        if family is dist.Beta
        else {"loc": 0.0, "scale": 1.0}
    )
    one = family(**{k: jnp.full((1,), v) for k, v in kw.items()})
    two = family(**{k: jnp.full((2,), v) for k, v in kw.items()})
    spec = _masked_spec(
        mask=jnp.array([True, False]), obs=jnp.array([0.4, 0.0]), family=family
    )
    masked = two.mask(spec.mask).log_prob(spec.obs).sum()
    assert float(masked) == pytest.approx(float(one.log_prob(jnp.array([0.4])).sum()))
```

## 1618. test_masking_does_not_introduce_a_companion_unobserved_site

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_e2_grid_membership_and_mask.py:226](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_e2_grid_membership_and_mask.py:226)

```python
@needs("E2", TypeError)
def test_masking_does_not_introduce_a_companion_unobserved_site() -> None:
    """``.mask()`` rather than ``obs_mask=``: one site per bundle.

    ``obs_mask`` would auto-generate ``{name}_unobserved``, a latent site the
    bundle layout has no offsets for and the gather would not know to skip. The
    indicator node stays ours instead -- which is also what keeps it available
    to be given parents later.
    """
    import numpyro
    from numpyro import handlers

    spec = _masked_spec(mask=jnp.array([True, False]), obs=jnp.array([0.4, 0.0]))

    def model():
        numpyro.sample("obs_site", spec.build(**spec.params).mask(spec.mask), obs=spec.obs)

    with handlers.seed(rng_seed=0), handlers.trace() as tr:
        model()
    assert set(tr) == {"obs_site"}
```

## 1620. test_a_fully_observed_and_a_partly_observed_member_share_one_bundle

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_e2_grid_membership_and_mask.py:248](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_e2_grid_membership_and_mask.py:248)

```python
@needs("E2", TypeError)
def test_a_fully_observed_and_a_partly_observed_member_share_one_bundle() -> None:
    """An all-True mask is the ordinary case, so masking does not split bundles.

    This is why the mask does not join the coalescing key: membership is still
    ``(indicator, source, unit)`` and the family, exactly as ``bundle_layout``
    already enforces. Two members differing only in how much of their grid was
    observed still belong together.
    """
    from digital_readiness.core.site_spec import bundle_layout
```

```python
@needs("E3", AttributeError)
def test_one_bundle_site_can_mix_literal_and_fill_cells() -> None:
    """Inside one site, cell A can be literal while cell B is a fill.

    Needs E1's identity key on the cell. Fails today before that exists.
    """
    from digital_readiness.core import observations as obs_mod
    from digital_readiness.core.observations import Observations

    a = ObservationCell(
        indicator="cov_3g", source="itu", year=2020, unit=("pct",)
    )
    b = ObservationCell(
        indicator="cov_3g", source="itu", year=2021, unit=("pct",)
    )
    obs = Observations(
        rules=(
            obs_mod.MemberLiteral(member=a.identity, value=jnp.array(0.4)),
            obs_mod.MemberFill(member=b.identity, value=0.0),
        )
    )
    assert obs.value_for_member(a.identity) == pytest.approx(0.4)
    filled = obs.value_for_member(b.identity, shape=())
    assert filled == pytest.approx(0.0)
```

```python
def _run_through(stage: str, cfg: GraphConfig):
    """Drive a data-free config up to and including ``stage``."""
    graph = build_graph(cfg)
    if stage == "compile":
        return compile_model(graph)
    if stage == "build":
        return graph
    raise AssertionError(f"unknown stage {stage!r}")
```

```python
@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", CASES, ids=lambda c: c.filename)
def test_adversarial_config(case: Case, _registry) -> None:
    cfg = _load(case.filename)
    if case.fails_with is None:
        # Generality fix has landed: the config must now run clean through stage.
        _run_through(case.stage, cfg)
        return
    exc_type, match = case.fails_with
    with pytest.raises(exc_type, match=match):
        _run_through(case.stage, cfg)
```

## 1636. test_every_example_config_is_accounted_for

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_example_configs.py:202](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_example_configs.py:202)

```python
def test_every_example_config_is_accounted_for() -> None:
    on_disk = {p.name for p in EXAMPLES.glob("*.yaml")}
    # "pinned by its own test" and "deliberately not run" are contradictory
    # claims, so a config in both sets is a filing error rather than redundancy.
    both = RUNNABLE_ELSEWHERE & TRACKED_UNTESTED
    assert not both, (
        "config(s) classified as both RUNNABLE_ELSEWHERE and TRACKED_UNTESTED: "
        f"{sorted(both)}"
    )
    classified = {c.filename for c in CASES} | RUNNABLE_ELSEWHERE | TRACKED_UNTESTED
    unclassified = on_disk - classified
    missing = classified - on_disk
    assert not unclassified, (
        "example config(s) not accounted for by A4 — add to CASES (adversarial), "
        "RUNNABLE_ELSEWHERE (has its own test), or TRACKED_UNTESTED (kept but "
        f"deliberately not run): {sorted(unclassified)}"
    )
    assert not missing, (
        f"A4 references example config(s) that no longer exist: {sorted(missing)}"
    )
```

```python
@needs("F2", TypeError)
def test_a_second_segmentation_family_can_register_for_the_walk() -> None:
    """Falsifier: G's family shape is declarable without editing the walk body.

    Registers a probe constructor with a ``time`` structural axis (I1) and a
    segmentation anchor. Fails today if register rejects ``structural_axes``
    or the walk cannot see a second family. Does not require the temporal CPD
    itself (that is G2).
    """

    def _fn(**_kwargs):  # pragma: no cover
        raise AssertionError("probe constructor should not run")

    register_cpd(
        "temporal_segmentation",
        "linear",
        _fn,
        kind="stochastic",
        structural_axes=(
            {
                "name": "year",
                "axis_role": "time",
                "level_source": "config_axes",
            },
        ),
        segmentation_anchor={
            "output_axis_hyperparameter": "n_segments",
            "output_length_from_k": "identity",
        },
    )
    entry = REGISTRY["temporal_segmentation"]["linear"]
    assert entry.segmentation_anchor is not None
    axes = getattr(entry, "structural_axes", None)
    assert axes is not None
    names = [
        (a["name"] if isinstance(a, dict) else a.name) for a in axes
    ]
    assert "year" in names
```

```python
@needs("F4", AssertionError)
def test_build_graph_skips_infer_structural_axes_on_v4() -> None:
    """v4 build must not call ``_infer_structural_axes`` even with an anchor.

    Uses the shipped v4 segmentation example (has an anchor). Infer runs before
    data-ref resolution, so a later ``UnresolvedDataRef`` is fine -- we only
    count calls. Today the helper still runs; F4 gates it to ``version < 4``.
    """
    from pathlib import Path

    from ruamel.yaml import YAML

    from digital_readiness.io import config as config_pkg
    from digital_readiness.io.config.schema import UnresolvedDataRef

    calls: list[int] = []
    original = build_mod._infer_structural_axes

    def _probe(*args, **kwargs):
        calls.append(1)
        return original(*args, **kwargs)

    path = (
        Path(config_pkg.__file__).parent / "examples" / "segmentation_child_v4.yaml"
    )
    cfg = GraphConfig.model_validate(YAML().load(path.read_text()))
    assert cfg.version == 4

    build_mod._infer_structural_axes = _probe  # type: ignore[assignment]
    try:
        try:
            build_graph(cfg)
        except UnresolvedDataRef:
            pass
    finally:
        build_mod._infer_structural_axes = original  # type: ignore[assignment]

    assert calls == [], (
        f"_infer_structural_axes ran {len(calls)} time(s) on v4 segmentation; "
        "F4 gates it to ≤v3"
    )
```

```python
@needs("F5", AssertionError)
def test_two_segmentation_anchors_are_an_error_not_silent_first_wins() -> None:

    # If the finder still returns only one without error, that is the bug.
    anchors = [
        n.id
        for n in cfg.nodes

        and build_mod.registry_entry_for(n.cpd) is not None

        # retarget this call.
```

```python
@needs("F5", AssertionError)
def test_continuation_ratio_finder_unused_on_v4_build_path() -> None:
    """v4 build must not call ``_find_continuation_ratio_anchor``.

    Source scan: the call is already gated ``version < 4`` nearby -- this pin
    requires that gate (or deletion). Today a call exists under version < 4;
    fail if an unguarded call appears for all versions.
    """
    src = (_REPO / "io/config/build.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    # Unguarded pattern would be a bare call without version nearby in the
    # assignment of shares_anchor.
    if "shares_anchor = _find_continuation_ratio_anchor" in src:
        idx = src.index("shares_anchor = _find_continuation_ratio_anchor")
        window = src[idx : idx + 200]
        if "version" not in window and "version < 4" not in src[idx - 80 : idx + 200]:
            raise AssertionError(
                "continuation-ratio finder call is not version-gated"
            )
    # If the helper is gone, F5 deletion half is done -- pass by absence.
    if not hasattr(build_mod, "_find_continuation_ratio_anchor"):
        return
    # Still present: require the v4 path does not invoke it.
    calls: list[int] = []
    original = build_mod._find_continuation_ratio_anchor

    def _probe(*args, **kwargs):
        calls.append(1)
        return original(*args, **kwargs)

    build_mod._find_continuation_ratio_anchor = _probe  # type: ignore[assignment]
    try:
        cfg = GraphConfig.model_validate(
            {
                "version": 4,
                "axes": {"country": {"kind": "categorical", "levels": ["US"]}},
                "nodes": [
                    {
                        "id": "x",
                        "cpd": {
                            "family": "beta",
                            "constructor": "prior",
                            "hyperparameters": {
                                "alpha": 1.0,
                                "beta": 1.0,
                                "axes": ["country"],
                            },
                        },
                    }
                ],
                "edges": [],
            }
        )
        build_graph(cfg)
    finally:
        build_mod._find_continuation_ratio_anchor = original  # type: ignore[assignment]

    assert calls == [], (
        "v4 build still called _find_continuation_ratio_anchor; "
        "F5 removes it from the v4 path"
    )
```

## 1678. test_constraint_zeros_need_no_graph_axes

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_fit_evidence.py:23](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_fit_evidence.py:23)

```python
def test_constraint_zeros_need_no_graph_axes(_registry) -> None:
    """The fill claims constraint sinks by name and reads no axes at all (A2).

    This test used to be ``test_constraint_zeros_infer_shape_from_lower_parent``,
    and it pinned the archaeology roadmap phase A2 removes: find the ``lower``
    parent through ``parameter_bindings``, read its ``axes``, drop whichever axis
    ``lower_spec`` reduces, and assert the resulting ``(2, 1, 2)``. That shape is
    still checked -- but where it is actually known, against a live distribution
    (``tests/inference/test_sample_wrapper.py::
    test_fill_rule_conditions_at_the_sites_own_shape``), and end to end through
    the ≤v3 MAP baseline. What is pinned *here* is the property that replaced it:
    the producer cannot get a shape wrong, because it never computes one.

    The graph below is kept verbatim from that test, ``lower_spec`` and all, so
    the case that most exercised the old inference is the case now shown not to
    need it.
    """
    country = AxisMeta(name="country", levels=("A", "B"), kind="categorical")
    year = AxisMeta(name="year", levels=(2024,), kind="ordinal")
    gender = AxisMeta(name="gender", levels=("F", "M"), kind="categorical")
    segment = AxisMeta(name="segment", levels=("S1", "S2", "S3", "S4"), kind="ordinal")

    g = BayesGraph()
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="segment_shares",
            kind="deterministic",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="continuation_ratio",
                hyperparameters={"axes": (country, year, gender, segment)},
            ),
        )
    )
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="cov_3g",
            kind="prior",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="beta",
                hyperparameters={"axes": (country, year)},
            ),
        )
    )
    g.add_node(
        NodeMeta(
            node_id="constraint_3g",
            kind="constraint_v0",
            cpd_spec=CpdSpec(
                family="bernoulli",
                hyperparameters={
                    "lower_spec": {"axis": "segment", "levels": ("S3", "S4")},
                    "tightness": 50.0,
                },
                parameter_bindings={
                    "lower": ("segment_shares",),
                    "upper": ("cov_3g",),
                },
            ),
        )
    )
    g.add_edge("segment_shares", "constraint_3g")
    g.add_edge("cov_3g", "constraint_3g")

    rule = constraint_zeros_from_graph(g)
    assert rule.sites() == frozenset({"constraint_3g"})
    assert rule.value == 0.0

    # Asked with the shape the old code went to the graph to derive, the rule
    # answers at exactly that shape -- and asked with a different one, it answers
    # at that one instead. Both are the same rule: it holds a constant, not an
    # array, so there is no stored shape to disagree with the site.
    assert rule.value_for("constraint_3g", (2, 1, 2)).shape == (2, 1, 2)
    assert rule.value_for("constraint_3g", (7,)).shape == (7,)
    assert jnp.all(rule.value_for("constraint_3g", (2, 1, 2)) == 0)

    # And the case the old code raised on outright: strip every axis off the
    # lower parent. Shape inference had nothing to work from and said so; the
    # rule does not care, because the sampler will supply the shape.
    g.get("segment_shares").cpd_spec.hyperparameters.pop("axes")
    assert constraint_zeros_from_graph(g).sites() == frozenset({"constraint_3g"})
```

## 1699. test_config_serializer_round_trips_desugared_yaml

**Unlabeled (test/support)**

[tests/io/test_h10_ruling13_falsifier.py:52](/Users/carlstone/digital-planet/digital_readiness/tests/io/test_h10_ruling13_falsifier.py:52)

```python
@needs("C5", AttributeError)
def test_config_serializer_round_trips_desugared_yaml() -> None:
    """Needs C5: serialize(desugar(cfg)) loads field-stable.

    Marked ``C5``, not ``H10``: the only thing this test needs that does not yet
    exist is the serializer, and a pin whose step id names a later phase does not
    clear when its actual dependency lands.

    *Corrected 2026-08-14.* This originally read
    ``from digital_readiness.io.config.desugar import serialize_config``, while C5's
    own pins mandated ``io.config``. Both sides xfailed with ``ImportError``, so the
    disagreement was invisible -- and had C5 landed at its mandated home, this test
    would have gone on raising ``ImportError``, staying xfail, looking correctly
    pinned, and never once exercising the ruling-13 round trip it exists for. The
    import-home question then dissolved: C5 was re-pinned as a method on the config,
    so there is no module to name.
    """
    cfg = GraphConfig.model_validate(YAML().load(_SEG.read_text()))
    flat = desugar(cfg)
    again = GraphConfig.model_validate(YAML().load(flat.serialize("yaml")))
    assert again.model_dump() == flat.model_dump()
```
